Requirements: Admission to the minor is by portfolio review and faculty interview only. To be considered for admission, students must be in good academic standing and have a minimum 2.0 cumulative GPA. No additional materials are required other than the portfolio. Application forms and deadlines are available in the Cinematic Arts Student Services Office, SCA 120. Note: Admission to all Cinematic Arts minors is on a competitive basis.
Department: USC School of Cinematic Arts
Description: The 3-D Animation in Cinematic Arts Minor offers students an opportunity to learn a broad range of skills and techniques related to 3-D computer animation. The goal of the minor is to foster talented artists and animators to create compelling animation, from conceptualization to modeling, rigging, animation and rendering. The minor is a useful supplement to a wide array of majors, from those within the cinematic arts, such as visual effects, animation and games, to those within engineering, such as computer science, and to majors within the fine arts, such as painting, drawing and photography, and beyond. This minor is not available to students in the BA in Animation and Digital Arts, the BFA in Animation and Digital Arts or the BS in Computer Science (Games) programs.

Department: Roski School of Art and Design
Description: The minor in 3-Dimensional Design teaches the language of form as a foundation for understanding the aesthetic, functional and structural concerns of three-dimensional objects and spaces. Through a range of projects and media, students develop skills in observation, conceptualization, and representation of 3-D forms in both physical and digital modes. The minor also provides an opportunity to develop an understanding of the relationship of 3-D design to its history and to the larger contexts of art and society.

Department: Leventhal School of Accounting
Description: The Accounting Minor is designed for students outside of the Leventhal School of Accounting who desire an understanding of the concepts and principles of accounting. This minor provides a foundational knowledge of accounting crucial for understanding business operations and financial health. Students will gain insights into financial reporting, managerial accounting, and the role of accounting information in decision-making, equipping them with valuable skills applicable across various industries and professions.
Accredidation: The Marshall School of Business and Leventhal School of Accounting are accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Addiction Science minor is designed for students interested in a career in public health, health care, social work, public policy, or medicine, with a particular focus on addiction and related issues. Students learn to recognize substance use disorders and addictive behaviors in various populations, how to implement evidence-based screening and prevention strategies across diverse settings, and develop a foundational understanding of the biological, psychological, and sociological underpinnings of addiction. Students also examine the role of public policy, epidemiology, and health services in addressing addiction and health equity. Graduates will gain expertise in addressing this critical public health issue from multiple perspectives and will be equipped to make a meaningful impact in their chosen professional path.

Requirements: Open to all USC undergraduates. Students interested in applying for this minor must have a minimum 2.5 USC GPA. Enrollment is limited, and students must apply through the Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism. Students interested in applying for this minor must apply online. Applications for fall admission are due on May 15, and applications for spring admission are due on December 15. Students interested in applying should contact their home department advisor, then schedule an appointment with an Annenberg academic advisor.
Department: USC Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
Description: The Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism offers an interdisciplinary minor in advertising that prepares students for careers in the dynamic field of advertising. The minor introduces students to the principles and practices of advertising through a blend of courses in communication, business, and design. Students learn about advertising strategy, media planning, creative development, and consumer insights, gaining a comprehensive understanding of the advertising industry. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical knowledge and practical skills, preparing students to develop effective advertising campaigns in a rapidly evolving media landscape.

Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: A dynamic interdisciplinary major focused on the experiences, history, culture, and intellectual traditions of African peoples throughout the world.

Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: This interdisciplinary minor introduces students to the study of race and ethnicity in the United States and the Americas. The program encourages students to analyze the history and contemporary experience of racial and ethnic groups in the United States, and to consider the theoretical, political, and cultural implications of race and ethnicity as categories of analysis in American society. Students will develop an understanding of various historical periods, cultural forms, and social movements, as well as the interplay of race, gender, class, and sexuality. Course work can include topics such as Native American studies, African American studies, Asian American studies, Chicano/Latino studies, and comparative ethnic studies.

Requirements: The department is seeking applicants with a strong academic background, a clear sense of purpose, and intellectual maturity. In addition to meeting the university requirements for graduate admission, applicants must submit the following: Official Transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, Statement of Purpose, Three letters of recommendation, Writing Sample (e.g., a term paper, thesis chapter, or professional paper on a topic related to the applicant's research interests. Minimum 15 pages in length.) and Curriculum Vitae (CV). GRE scores are not required for admission to the Anthropology Ph.D. program.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Ph.D. program in Anthropology (Visual Anthropology) at the University of Southern California has been in existence since 1983. It is designed to train students in the analysis of visual systems and the production of visual media, including ethnographic film, photography, and new media. It is unique in its integration of theoretical training in anthropology with professional training in ethnographic media production. Visual anthropology focuses on the study of culture through visual modalities (e.g. ethnographic film, photography, new media, performance, architecture, the built environment) and, relatedly, on the study of how people communicate through such media, and how anthropologists might represent culture using them. In keeping with this, faculty in visual anthropology teach and train students in critical approaches to analyzing and making visual media, and in using visual media to communicate ethnographic knowledge and theory. We train students in theory, methods, and the history of visual anthropology; they produce a visual ethnographic project in addition to a written dissertation. The program encourages interdisciplinary work with other departments at USC, including Cinema, Art History, and American Studies and Ethnicity.

Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The minor in Asian American Studies introduces students to the experiences of Asian Americans through an interdisciplinary approach that considers issues of race, gender, sexuality, ethnicity, and class in historical and contemporary contexts. The minor aims to provide students with a critical understanding of the forces that have shaped Asian American communities and how Asian Americans have responded to and resisted these forces. The minor prepares students to engage with a diverse society and to become advocates for social justice.

Requirements: A minimum of 20 units is required for the minor. All courses must be taken for a letter grade. All students must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 in the courses taken for the minor. Courses applied to the minor may not be taken on a pass/no pass basis. All minor coursework must be taken at USC.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: A growing body of research suggests that psychological factors influence economic behavior, decision-making, and market outcomes. The minor in Behavioral Economics and Psychology introduces students to foundational knowledge in both fields as they relate to and integrate with one another. Students will gain an understanding of the cognitive, social, and emotional factors that influence individual decision-making, as well as an understanding of how these factors can lead to deviations from traditional economic models. The minor provides students with an interdisciplinary perspective on human behavior, equipping them with valuable analytical tools applicable to various fields, including public policy, marketing, finance, and organizational behavior.

Requirements: To apply for the USC DPT program, you must complete the USC Graduate Application and the Physical Therapist Centralized Application Service (PTCAS) application. These applications are separate and require different materials and deadlines. Required Application Materials include: Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended; Three letters of recommendation; GRE scores are NOT required for the 2024 application cycle; TOEFL or IELTS scores (for international applicants); Personal Statement; Observation Hours Verification (at least 150 hours of physical therapy observation, volunteer, or work experience, completed in at least two different settings, one of which must be inpatient and one outpatient. All hours must be verified.); USC Graduate Application.
Department: Division of Biokinesiology and Physical Therapy
MinimumGreScore: Verbal above 153, Quantitative above 144, Analytical Writing above 4

Requirements: Applicants must submit materials both to USC and to the department. The Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) general test is required. Additional required documents for graduate admission include a Statement of Purpose, Letters of Recommendation, and Transcripts. Official GRE scores must be submitted directly to USC from ETS, institution code 4852. International applicants must also satisfy English proficiency requirements.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Biophysics program is housed in the Department of Biological Sciences. It is an interdisciplinary program designed to train students for careers in biophysics research. The program emphasizes the application of quantitative approaches to biological problems and provides students with a strong foundation in physics, mathematics, and biology, as well as hands-on research experience.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Fellowships, Assistantships, Federal Loans, Federal Work-Study

Requirements: Applications are accepted for fall admission only. All applicants must meet the general admission requirements of the USC Graduate School. In addition to these requirements, applicants must submit: a statement of purpose, a writing sample (15-25 pages), letters of recommendation (3), official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, GRE General Test scores (optional).
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Central European Studies minor provides students with an understanding of Central Europe (Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary) from a multidisciplinary perspective, including literature, film, history, political science and culture. Students will learn about the region’s rich history and complex present and gain an understanding of its important role in contemporary Europe.

Requirements: Applicants must submit either the Common Application or Coalition Application, which includes essay prompts, along with the USC Writing Supplement. Required documents include official high school transcripts, a counselor recommendation, and a teacher recommendation. Standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional for the 2024, 2025, and 2026 application cycles. Additional financial aid documents are required for those applying for financial assistance.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Chicano/Latino Studies program offers an interdisciplinary curriculum that explores the experiences of Chicana/os and Latina/os in the United States and transnational contexts. Students examine the historical, political, social, economic, and cultural forces that have shaped and continue to shape Chicana/o and Latina/o communities. The program offers a broad understanding of Chicana/o and Latina/o communities from a comparative, critical, and interdisciplinary perspective. The BA in Chicano/Latino Studies is ideal for students interested in careers in law, public policy, education, social work, journalism, and community organizing, as well as those pursuing graduate studies in the humanities and social sciences. Students develop critical thinking, analytical, and communication skills, preparing them to address complex social issues and contribute to diverse communities.

Requirements: Applicants to the MA in Computational Linguistics program are expected to have a bachelor's degree in linguistics, computer science, or a related field. Students from other backgrounds will be considered if they have completed substantial coursework in linguistics or computer science, as well as a demonstrated interest in the field. Applicants must submit the following materials: Official transcripts from all universities attended, Statement of purpose, Three letters of recommendation, GRE General Test scores (optional), Resume or curriculum vitae, A writing sample (optional), International applicants must also submit TOEFL or IELTS scores. See the USC Graduate Admission website for additional information regarding minimum scores. Specific requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0. A strong academic record, particularly in linguistics, computer science, mathematics, or related fields. Background in basic programming and data structures is desirable. Background in formal linguistics (syntax, semantics, phonology) is desirable.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The minor in computational linguistics, offered jointly by the Department of Linguistics and the Department of Computer Science, focuses on theoretical and practical aspects of language technology. The program provides students with a solid background in both linguistics and computer science and prepares them for further study or entry-level positions in areas such as natural language processing, information retrieval, machine translation, and speech recognition.

Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The PhD in Computational Neuroscience is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide students with a broad background in theoretical and computational approaches to neuroscience. Students will develop a strong foundation in the mathematical and computational tools necessary to understand the brain's complex functions, from the molecular and cellular level to systems and cognitive processes. The program emphasizes both theoretical understanding and practical application, preparing graduates for research careers in academia or industry.
MinimumGreScore: above the 50th percentile on all three sections of the exam
ScholarshipType: Full financial aid (stipend, tuition remission, health benefits)

ProgramName: Contemporary Latino and Latin American Studies
Requirements:
Applicants for the M.A. in Contemporary Latino and Latin American Studies are expected to have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must submit the following:

Online application
Transcripts from all colleges and universities attended
A statement of purpose (1,000–1,500 words). The statement of purpose should explain how the applicant’s academic and professional experiences have prepared them for graduate study in Contemporary Latino and Latin American Studies, and how this program will help them achieve their future goals.
Three letters of recommendation from faculty members or others qualified to evaluate the applicant’s academic and professional potential.
A writing sample (20–25 pages). The writing sample should be an academic paper, preferably one that focuses on topics related to the CLALS program.
GRE General Test scores are not required.
A current résumé or curriculum vitae (CV).

International applicants must submit a score of 90 on the TOEFL or 6.5 on the IELTS. For a list of eligible exemptions, please see the USC Graduate Admissions website: gradadm.usc.edu.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The minor in Contemporary Latino and Latin American Studies provides students with an interdisciplinary understanding of the historical, social, political, economic and cultural experiences of Latina/os in the United States, as well as those of peoples and nations throughout Latin America and the Caribbean. The minor allows students to apply the analytical tools and perspectives of the humanities and social sciences to the study of a vibrant and increasingly influential demographic in the United States, and to explore the challenges and opportunities for transnational exchange and collaboration with Latin American societies. The minor also helps students prepare for graduate work in area studies or related fields such as sociology, political science, history, literature and anthropology, as well as for careers in public policy, government, law, education, business, journalism, social work, and community organizing.
ScholarshipType: Federal, State, Institutional (Fellowships, Grants, Assistantships), Outside Scholarships

Requirements: Required Application Materials: Official transcripts from all institutions attended, Résumé/CV, Statement of Purpose, Three letters of recommendation, GRE scores (Optional for Fall 2024 and Spring 2025 applicants), Proof of English proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE) for international applicants.
Department: Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: The Data Science program provides graduate students with the interdisciplinary knowledge and skills needed to manage and analyze large datasets. Students will develop a strong foundation in areas such as machine learning, data mining, statistical modeling, and data visualization. The program emphasizes both theoretical understanding and practical application, preparing graduates for careers in diverse fields including technology, finance, healthcare, and research.

Requirements: A complete application includes: Your application, including essays, short answers and activities list. Official high school transcripts. Optional: Standardized Test Scores (SAT/ACT). Letters of Recommendation (not required but recommended).
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Data Science is an interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers that require both economic analysis and data science skills. This program provides students with a strong foundation in economic theory and quantitative methods, as well as the computational and statistical skills necessary to analyze large datasets. Students will learn how to apply economic principles to real-world problems using modern data science techniques, including machine learning, econometrics, and data visualization. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and the ethical considerations of data analysis. Upon completion of the Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Data Science, students will be able to: Demonstrate a strong understanding of economic theory and quantitative methods. Apply data science techniques to analyze economic data, including machine learning and econometrics. Communicate economic insights effectively through data visualization and written reports. Evaluate the ethical implications of data collection and analysis.

Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Economics/Mathematics offers students the opportunity to combine serious study in both disciplines. Students interested in quantitative approaches to economics and economic theory, as well as those planning to pursue graduate study in economics, mathematics or related fields, will find this major particularly appropriate. The Economics/Mathematics curriculum is designed to provide students with: 1. A solid foundation in microeconomics and macroeconomics. 2. A strong foundation in mathematical methods. 3. An understanding of statistics and econometrics and their applications. 4. The ability to use quantitative methods to analyze economic problems. 5. Critical thinking and problem-solving skills.

Requirements: The Common Application or Coalition Application, USC Writing Supplement, Official High School Transcripts, SAT or ACT scores, Letters of Recommendation (up to 2).
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: Students in the Environmental Science and Health major examine the scientific basis of environmental problems and their impact on human health. They gain a solid foundation in environmental chemistry, earth sciences, life sciences and quantitative methods, as well as an understanding of the social and public policy aspects of environmental problems and human health. The major emphasizes quantitative and analytical skills and prepares students for careers or graduate study in environmental science, environmental health, public health, environmental consulting, and environmental policy and law.

Requirements: Applicants must complete the USC Undergraduate Application (Common Application or Coalition Application), including the USC Writing Supplement (short answer questions, an essay of about 250 words, and a list of activities and honors). Official transcripts and one letter of recommendation from a counselor or teacher are required. SAT or ACT scores are optional for Fall 2023 and Fall 2024 applicants. Additionally, for the Film & Television Production program, supplemental materials must be submitted through SlideRoom, which include a Creative Introduction (90-second video), a Visual Sample, a Written Sample (maximum 5 pages), and a list of creative work.
Department: USC School of Cinematic Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Film & Television Production is an intensive program of study in the theory and practice of producing, directing, writing, cinematography, editing, sound, and interactive media. Students gain experience through the creation of a range of projects from traditional narratives and documentaries to interactive and experimental forms. Emphasis is placed on collaboration and creative leadership throughout the filmmaking process. The program develops filmmakers who are original storytellers capable of working across all mediums. Upon graduation, students have a portfolio of work and the skills to enter the film and television industry.

Requirements: Common Application; USC Writing Supplement; Counselor recommendation and school report; Teacher recommendation; High school transcript(s); SAT or ACT scores (optional for 2024, 2025, 2026 application cycles); Mid-year senior year transcript (if available)
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: Undergraduate instruction in French is designed to acquaint students with the language, literatures, and cultures of France and the French-speaking world. In addition to language training, course work covers French and Francophone literatures and cultures, literary and critical theory, film, history, and the history of ideas. Students develop skills in critical analysis, analytical and argumentative writing, and oral expression.

Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: A joint major is offered in French and Italian. A total of 32 units beyond French 200 or 220 and Italian 200 or 220 are required. Students must complete 16 units in French beyond French 200 or 220, including French 300, 320 and 370. They must also complete 16 units in Italian beyond Italian 200 or 220, including Italian 300, 320 and 370.

Requirements: All applicants must apply online through the Common Application. Applicants should submit high school transcripts for all high school work, standardized test scores (if they wish), essays and letters of recommendation. Specific majors may require additional materials.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Gender and Sexuality Studies provides students with the opportunity to pursue an interdisciplinary course of study that examines the intersections of gender, sexuality, race, class, religion, and nation in diverse global and historical contexts. Through an exploration of cutting-edge scholarship, students develop analytical skills and critical perspectives on social justice issues, preparing them for careers in fields such as law, education, public policy, health, social work, journalism, and the arts, as well as for graduate study. This program offers students an opportunity to explore a variety of methods and approaches to feminist and queer scholarship, with a particular strength in transnational and postcolonial feminist approaches. A unique strength of the program is its integration of theory and practice through community-based learning opportunities in Los Angeles. The GSS BA also emphasizes the interdisciplinary nature of the field by allowing students to complete coursework in other departments.
ScholarshipType: Full funding package (tuition waiver, health insurance, annual stipend)

Department: Spatial Sciences Institute (Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences)
Fees: 74,336 USD for the program (32 units) (based on 2023-2024 tuition rate)
CollegeApplicationFee: 74,336 USD for the program (32 units) (based on 2023-2024 tuition rate)

Requirements: Applicants for the MS and PhD degrees are expected to have a bachelor’s degree in geological sciences or a related field (e.g., biology, chemistry, computer science, engineering, environmental sciences, mathematics, or physics). All applicants are required to submit a statement of purpose, a current resume or curriculum vitae, and three letters of recommendation. The GRE General Test is not required. International applicants must also satisfy the English proficiency requirements specified in the Graduate and Postdoctoral Scholar Programs Bulletin.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Geological Sciences requires a minimum of 60 units of graduate work beyond the bachelor’s degree, or 48 units beyond the master’s degree. Students are encouraged to pursue an individualized program of study in consultation with their faculty adviser. The degree prepares students for research and teaching careers in academia or research careers in industry or government. Students must choose an area of specialization from those listed below under Areas of Study. Students may take courses from other departments when appropriate. A qualifying exam, a dissertation proposal and a dissertation defense are required. Teaching assistantships are a normal part of the PhD training. Requirements for the PhD degree are intended to be completed in four to five years, though the time will vary from student to student.
ScholarshipType: Full financial support (includes stipend, tuition, and fees)

Requirements: Online Application, Application Fee, Transcripts, GRE General Test: Not Required, Resume/CV: Required, Statement of Purpose: Required, Letters of Recommendation: Required (3 letters), Writing Sample: Not Required, Portfolio: Optional, English Proficiency: Required for international students (TOEFL, IELTS, PTE).
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The USC Global Geodesign graduate certificate is designed to provide professional training for students and practitioners who are working to understand and analyze complex environmental and social issues to propose design solutions that address these challenges locally and globally. Geodesign is an emerging practice that bridges geographic information systems (GIS) and planning and design in an interactive process, integrating geographic science and analysis with design practice, providing an iterative workflow that uses scientific information to inform design proposals. The 12-unit certificate is an interdisciplinary program that draws from the fields of spatial sciences, landscape architecture, and urban planning. The certificate is offered primarily online, with an optional one-week, in-person design charrette studio at the end of the summer session.

Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The minor in Health and Humanity focuses on the social, cultural, and historical dimensions of health and healing. The program introduces students to critical approaches to the study of health and medicine, and prepares them to understand the diverse ways that different societies and cultures define, understand, and address issues of health and disease. Through the minor, students learn to contextualize contemporary health challenges, to appreciate the variety of medical traditions, and to understand the role of healing in human society. The minor draws on the insights and methods of a wide range of humanistic and social science disciplines, including anthropology, history, literature, philosophy, psychology, religious studies, and sociology. The minor is a valuable complement to majors in the natural sciences, public health, and other health-related fields, as well as to majors in the humanities and social sciences. The minor also helps prepare students for careers in health care, public health, health policy, and related fields.

Requirements: First-year applicants must submit: Common Application; the USC Writing Supplement, which includes several short answer questions and two short essays; a Counselor Recommendation; a Teacher Recommendation; official High School Transcript; and Mid-Year Grades. Standardized Test Scores (SAT/ACT) are optional for fall 2024 and fall 2025 first-year applicants. A Portfolio or Audition may be required for specific majors.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Health and Human Sciences provides a scientific and interdisciplinary foundation for students interested in careers related to health, human behavior and the human body. The curriculum emphasizes the biological, behavioral and social sciences, and prepares students for a wide variety of entry-level positions in health-related fields, or for further graduate or professional training.

Requirements: Admission to the USC Rossier School of Education is a highly selective process. The admissions committee considers many factors in evaluating candidates, including academic record, test scores, letters of recommendation, statement of purpose, and professional experience. All applicants are required to possess a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must also meet the minimum requirements for admission to the USC Graduate School. Required documents include: Application for Admission, Statement of Purpose, Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts, GRE (Graduate Record Examinations) Scores, English Proficiency (for international students), California Basic Educational Skills Test (CBEST), California Subject Examinations for Teachers (CSET), U.S. Citizenship (if applicable).
Department: Rossier School of Education
Description: The Master of Arts in Teaching (MAT) with a concentration in History and Social Science provides initial preparation for individuals seeking a California preliminary single subject teaching credential in History and Social Science. The USC Rossier School of Education offers this program. This program leads to a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Urban Education with a specialization in History and Social Science Education. This is an advanced degree for students who intend to pursue research careers as university faculty or in applied research organizations.

Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description:
Human Biology is the study of human life, incorporating knowledge from the biological and social sciences. The major emphasizes an evolutionary perspective on human biology, considering the origins and ramifications of human biological variation, adaptation, and behavior. The curriculum provides students with a strong background in general biology, human anatomy and physiology, genetics, development, ecology and evolution, and behavior. Graduates of the program will have a broad understanding of the scientific study of human biology, from genes to global populations, and are well prepared for careers in health professions, science, education, public health, and conservation, as well as graduate study in related fields.

Description and Learning Objectives:
Upon completion of the Human Biology BA program, students will be able to:
* Explain the basic principles of evolution and how they apply to human biology, behavior, and culture.
* Apply an understanding of human genetics, development, anatomy, and physiology to explain the function and variation of the human body.
* Explain the social, cultural, and ecological factors that influence human health, disease, and behavior.
* Evaluate scientific literature, analyze data, and communicate scientific findings effectively in both written and oral forms.
* Understand the ethical implications of biological research and its application to human society.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Restricted by donor criteria, Federal, State, Private, Departmental

Requirements: Applications are accepted for fall and spring semester admission. See here for a list of application deadlines. All applicants must have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must submit official transcripts from all institutions attended. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 is required. Applicants must also submit a statement of purpose and three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required for admission to the Human Security and Geospatial Intelligence program. An interview may be required.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences, Rossier School of Education
Description: The Master of Science in Human Security and Geospatial Intelligence (HSGI) provides students with knowledge and analytic capabilities to address critical issues related to human security, humanitarian intervention, and the uses of geospatial intelligence in these efforts. The interdisciplinary curriculum integrates the study of human security with geospatial intelligence concepts, tools, and practices, preparing students for careers in diverse sectors, including national and international government agencies, non-governmental organizations, and private companies.
ScholarshipType: Federal loans, work-study, departmental awards, research and teaching assistantships, fellowships, grants, private aid

Requirements: In addition to the requirements of the Graduate School, applicants must submit: The GRE General Test is required. Students who have a graduate degree from a U.S. institution or who are currently enrolled in a PhD program at USC are exempt from the GRE requirement. An average GRE score for admitted students is 155 verbal, 160 quantitative and 3.5 analytical writing. Only scores submitted electronically from ETS will be accepted. USC’s ETS institution code is 4852. Three letters of recommendation are required from faculty or supervisors. A resume is required. A statement of purpose is required. Official transcripts from all universities attended. Applicants whose native language is not English must submit scores for either the TOEFL or IELTS. See the USC Graduate Admission website for minimum score requirements.
Department: Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: The Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering provides an education that will prepare students to address the design and improvement of complex systems. The discipline uses mathematical, physical and social sciences together with engineering analysis and design to specify, predict and evaluate the results to be obtained from such systems. Emphasis is placed on the integration of people, materials, information, equipment and energy. Industrial and systems engineers work with technology, information and management in manufacturing and service industries. Students are required to take a minimum of 128 units.

Requirements: Application for Graduate Admission; Transcripts; Letters of Recommendation (3 required); GRE Scores (optional for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 applications); English Proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS); Resume/CV (Required); Statement of Purpose (Required).
Department: USC Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree in Intelligence and Cyber Operations is a rigorous, interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers in the intelligence community and various cyber operations roles within both government and the private sector. This program integrates a unique blend of technical skills, analytical methods, and strategic understanding, positioning graduates at the forefront of national security and cybersecurity challenges. The curriculum emphasizes foundational knowledge in computer science, cybersecurity, data analysis, and intelligence studies, coupled with practical training in ethical hacking, digital forensics, and threat intelligence. Students will develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills essential for effective performance in complex and rapidly evolving operational environments. Graduates will be equipped to tackle multifaceted challenges related to cyber espionage, counterterrorism, information warfare, and critical infrastructure protection.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based scholarships, Research Assistantships (RA), Teaching Assistantships (TA)

Requirements: Online Application, Official Transcripts, Letters of Recommendation (3 required), Statement of Purpose, GRE General Test (optional for Fall 2024 applicants), English Language Proficiency (international applicants), CV/Resume
Department: School of International Relations
Description: The International Relations (Global Business) major provides students with a detailed understanding of the international political economy. It focuses on the political dynamics of international trade, finance, and business, as well as foreign policy, regional security, and international law and organization. The curriculum blends the strengths of USC Dornsife College’s International Relations program with USC Marshall School of Business’s expertise in global business. Students study political and economic theories, examine the global economic system through an international relations lens, and gain analytical skills necessary to evaluate the international business environment.

ProgramName: International Relations and the Global Economy
Requirements: Admission to the graduate programs in International Relations and the Global Economy requires a bachelor’s degree, a strong undergraduate record, and three letters of recommendation. The program requires satisfactory scores on the Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) General Test. USC international graduate applicants are also required to submit scores on the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or International English Language System (IELTS) exam.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: This major provides a comprehensive understanding of the international political economy, with an emphasis on the interaction between economic and political processes in a global context. It examines the major theories and current issues in international political economy, international trade, international finance, and economic development. Students pursuing this major will develop a strong analytical foundation for understanding global issues from an interdisciplinary perspective. The major prepares students for graduate studies in international relations, economics, business, and law, as well as for careers in international business, banking and finance, journalism, consulting, and government and non-governmental organizations.

Requirements: Common Application; USC Questions; High School Transcripts; Test Scores (SAT or ACT) — Optional for Fall 2024 Applicants; Recommendations; Portfolio, slide room, or audition (if applicable); Financial Aid Application
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: A minor in Italian allows students to gain proficiency in the Italian language and to study the literature and culture of Italy. Students must complete 20 units of coursework with a grade of C or better. A minimum of 20 units above ITAL 120, including a minimum of 8 units at the 300 level or above, is required for the minor.
ScholarshipAmount: from a few thousands dollars to full tuition

Requirements: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, High School Transcript, SAT or ACT scores (if submitted), Letter(s) of Recommendation, School Report, Mid-Year Report (if available)
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and and Sciences
Description: The minor in Jewish Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a comprehensive knowledge of the history, culture and religion of the Jewish people and Judaism. Students are exposed to a broad range of courses, from literature, history, religion and philosophy to sociology, political science and modern Hebrew language, and participate in academic and cultural events.

Requirements: Application to the doctoral program requires a bachelor’s degree, a superior academic record, and a statement of purpose. It also requires submission of a writing sample, three letters of recommendation, and official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. All international applicants must submit an official Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or International English Language Testing System (IELTS) score, unless they are exempt from the requirement.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The major in Latin American and Iberian Cultures offers an interdisciplinary approach to the cultures, literatures and civilizations of Latin America, Spain, Portugal and other Portuguese-speaking countries, and to the study of the Spanish and Portuguese languages. Students majoring in Latin American and Iberian Cultures are encouraged to study abroad in one of the approved programs in Latin America or Spain for one or two semesters. Contact the study abroad office (Doheny Memorial Library, DML 104) for a list of approved programs.

ProgramName: Latin American and Iberian Cultures, Media and Politics
Requirements: All students must complete the USC Core and satisfy a foreign language requirement at USC. See general requirements for undergraduate degrees.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The minor in Latin American and Iberian Cultures, Media and Politics offers students an interdisciplinary approach to the study of the cultures, media and politics of Latin America and the Iberian Peninsula (Spain and Portugal). The minor provides an opportunity to combine courses from areas such as Spanish, Portuguese, Latin American and Iberian Studies, Cinematic Arts, Political Science, International Relations, History, and Anthropology. Students will gain a deep understanding of the diverse histories, cultures, media, and political landscapes of these regions, while also enhancing their language skills (Spanish or Portuguese). The minor culminates in a capstone experience where students apply their knowledge to a specific research project, internship, or study abroad experience in the region.

Requirements: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, Transcripts. Standardized Test Scores (SAT/ACT) are not required for fall 2023, fall 2024 and fall 2025 applicants. Students who do not submit scores will not be disadvantaged in the admission process. Scores are required for some merit scholarship programs.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The minor in Law, History and Culture offers an interdisciplinary approach to the study of law, legal systems, and legal cultures from a humanities perspective. It provides students with critical insight into the historical development of law, legal institutions and legal theory, and with a nuanced understanding of the cultural and social effects of law. It also enables students to develop skills in the historical analysis of primary documents, and in the critical interpretation of legal texts and judicial opinions. The minor is a valuable complement to a variety of majors including international relations, political science, history, sociology, philosophy, and gender studies. The minor also provides an excellent basis for students considering graduate study in law or in the humanities. The Law, History and Culture minor is offered by the Department of History.

Requirements: Admission to graduate programs in Materials Science requires a bachelor’s degree in science or engineering. Students applying for admission should submit a complete application as described in the Viterbi Graduate School of Engineering section of this catalogue. All applicants must submit GRE General Test scores, official transcripts of all college work, letters of recommendation, and a statement of purpose. International applicants must also submit TOEFL or IELTS scores. Applications are due December 15 for fall admission and September 15 for spring admission.
Department: Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: Materials Science (MSCI) is an interdisciplinary field, drawing on the disciplines of physics, chemistry and engineering to understand the fundamental relationships between the processing, structure and properties of materials. This understanding is used to design new materials and to improve the performance of existing ones. Materials are a ubiquitous enabling technology for fields ranging from quantum computing to space exploration, and materials scientists are critical to solving grand challenges in energy, health, infrastructure, and sustainability. The Department of Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering offers programs of graduate study leading to the Master of Science (MS) in Materials Science and the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Materials Science.

Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Queer Arts and Culture Minor is designed for students interested in exploring the role of arts and culture in the formation of queer identities, communities, and social movements. This minor offers an interdisciplinary approach to studying the intersections of LGBTQ+ experiences with various artistic forms, cultural practices, and media. Students will engage with critical theories and historical perspectives to understand how queer artists and cultural producers have challenged norms, expressed dissent, and forged new ways of being and relating. The curriculum covers a range of topics including queer performance, film, literature, visual arts, and digital culture, encouraging students to analyze cultural texts and practices through a queer lens. The minor aims to foster analytical skills, creative thinking, and a deeper appreciation for the contributions of queer artists and cultural workers to broader society.

Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The minor in Race, Ethnicity, and Politics exposes students to the political study of race and ethnicity, especially the way in which race and ethnicity shape the behavior of political actors, political institutions, and political systems. The minor examines race and ethnicity in both American and comparative political contexts and provides students with a set of tools to analyze critically the role of race and ethnicity in political life.

Requirements: Admission to the doctoral program in Religion requires evidence of superior academic ability and preparation. While most successful applicants will have an M.A. in Religious Studies, candidates with a strong B.A. or with an M.A. in a related field will be considered. For admission to the PhD program, the following are required: completed online application, statement of purpose (1,000–1,500 words), academic writing sample (20–30 pages), official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, three letters of recommendation, official Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) scores (verbal, quantitative, and analytical writing), and international applicants must submit official scores from the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or International English Language Testing System (IELTS).
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Department of Religion offers courses on the major religious traditions of the world — Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, and Judaism — as well as on new religious movements and on ancient, indigenous, and non-Western religions. Courses address religion from a variety of disciplinary perspectives, including anthropology, critical theory, history, literary studies, philosophy, and sociology. Students learn to analyze and understand religious phenomena in diverse cultural and historical contexts and to evaluate critically the role of religion in human society, both past and present. Majors are trained in critical thinking, the analysis of complex cultural systems, and sophisticated expository writing.

ProgramName: Renaissance, Early Modern, and Reformation Studies Minor
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: This minor draws on the faculty and courses of a number of departments and programs to provide undergraduates with an interdisciplinary understanding of the period of the Renaissance, Early Modern, and Reformation eras (roughly 1400-1800). This period is one of extraordinary dynamism and change, which gave birth to many of the ideas, institutions, and practices of the modern world, as well as forms of cultural and aesthetic expression still vibrant today. Courses available will address the religious upheavals of the Reformation; the scientific revolution; the impact of the printing press; the rise of the nation-state and the international legal order; the development of the global economy and colonialism; the rise of capitalism; changes in gender and family structures; developments in art, architecture, music, and literary forms; and the impact of these developments on philosophy and political thought. Students completing the minor will emerge with a sophisticated understanding of the historical roots of many contemporary issues and problems, as well as a deeper appreciation of the complex cultural heritage that shapes our lives.

Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The minor in Russian introduces students to a major language, literature and culture of the world through coursework in Russian language, literature and culture. It is an excellent complement to majors in the humanities and social sciences. The minor also provides an excellent foundation for professional careers in government, journalism, international relations and law, and for graduate work in Russian or other fields.

Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The minor in Science, Technology, and Society (STS) gives students an interdisciplinary education in the ways that science and technology shape society and culture, and the ways that society and culture shape science and technology. Students in the minor will learn how to critically examine the assumptions, practices, and products of scientific and technological endeavors. The STS minor is structured to provide students with a solid intellectual foundation in the history, philosophy, and sociology of science and technology. Students will also learn to analyze scientific and technological controversies and the ethical, legal, political, and cultural aspects of scientific knowledge production and technological development. STS minors will also gain an understanding of science communication and the roles of expertise and publics in a democratic society.

Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Spanish minor introduces students to the language, culture, and civilization of the Spanish-speaking world. The minor improves students’ linguistic competency and expands their understanding of Spanish and Latin American cultures, which prepares them for a variety of professions in a global context.

Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Thematic Approaches to Culture minor is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a comprehensive understanding of human culture from various disciplinary perspectives. Through a flexible curriculum, students will explore cultural phenomena, expressions, and practices across different historical periods and geographical regions. The program aims to equip students with the analytical tools necessary to critically engage with diverse cultural forms, including literature, art, media, religion, and social movements. Students will develop critical thinking and research skills, learn to analyze cultural phenomena from multiple perspectives, and communicate their insights effectively. The minor is suitable for students from any major interested in deepening their understanding of the complexities of human culture.

Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Visual Culture Minor introduces students to the study of visuality as a central aspect of human experience. Drawing on a range of disciplinary perspectives—art history, critical theory, literature, media studies, performance studies, philosophy—the minor explores the social and cultural significance of images and visual practices across different historical periods and geographical locations. Students will develop critical tools to analyze how visual culture shapes identities, knowledge, power relations, and various forms of expression, from fine art and popular culture to digital media and scientific imaging. The curriculum emphasizes interdisciplinary approaches, encouraging students to engage with diverse visual forms and theoretical frameworks. Through coursework, students will enhance their ability to interpret complex visual phenomena, articulate informed arguments, and contribute to contemporary debates about the role of the visual in society.

Department: Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: The Web Technologies and Applications minor provides students with the fundamental knowledge and skills needed to design, develop, and deploy modern web-based applications. The minor emphasizes both the client-side (front-end) and server-side (back-end) aspects of web development, covering topics such as user interface design, web programming languages, database integration, and web security. Students will gain practical experience through hands-on projects, preparing them for careers in web development, software engineering, and related fields.

Requirements: Applicants for undergraduate programs at USC, including the Bachelor of Science in Accounting, must submit the Common Application with the USC Writing Supplement, official high school transcripts, a counselor recommendation, a teacher recommendation, and a Mid-Year Report. Standardized test scores (ACT or SAT) are optional for students applying for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 admission. The USC Marshall School of Business does not require supplemental essays, letters of recommendation, portfolios, or interviews.
Department: Leventhal School of Accounting
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Accounting is designed for students who are committed to a career in accounting. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in all areas of accounting, including financial accounting, managerial accounting, auditing, and taxation. Students also gain a broader understanding of business principles through courses in finance, marketing, and management. The program prepares graduates for entry-level positions in public accounting, corporate accounting, government, and non-profit organizations. It also provides an excellent foundation for pursuing graduate studies in accounting or related fields, such as law or business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Accounting and Finance
Requirements: All applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes the Common Application essay and the USC Writing Supplement (additional essays). Official transcripts from all secondary schools attended, and a letter of recommendation from a counselor and/or teacher are required. Standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 applicants. International students whose native language is not English must also submit TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE Academic scores.
Department: Marshall School of Business
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Accounting and Finance is a limited enrollment program designed to provide students with a strong foundation in both disciplines, preparing them for careers that require an integrated understanding of accounting and finance. This joint program, offered by the Leventhal School of Accounting and the Department of Finance and Business Economics, provides students with rigorous training in financial reporting, corporate finance, investments, and financial analysis. Graduates are well-prepared for roles in investment banking, corporate finance, asset management, and public accounting, as well as for further graduate studies.
ScholarshipType: Federal Pell Grants, Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grants (FSEOG), Cal Grants, USC Merit Scholarships, Restricted Scholarships

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Acting, Stage and Screen
Requirements: Applicants to the School of Dramatic Arts must apply through the Common Application. The required Application Supplement (via SlideRoom) is included within the Common Application. Once you have initiated your Common Application, you will receive information on how to access the SlideRoom Supplement, including instructions, requirements and deadlines. Applications are reviewed holistically, with emphasis placed on auditions, academic history, essays, letters of recommendation, and overall potential. All applicants must submit official transcripts. All applicants are highly encouraged to submit official standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) as part of their application. You will submit two letters of recommendation: one academic and one artistic. Required: Headshot, theatre resume (or resume of experience). Audition: Applicants will be considered for a live audition after the submission of the application. More details are available in the SlideRoom application. All applicants invited to audition will receive an email with specific audition requirements, date and time slots.
Department: USC School of Dramatic Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Acting, Stage and Screen program is a highly selective conservatory-style program designed for students seeking rigorous training in the craft of acting for theatre, film, and television. Students will develop a comprehensive set of acting skills, including voice, movement, scene study, improvisation, and script analysis. The curriculum also integrates foundational knowledge in theatre history, dramatic literature, and professional practices. Graduates will be prepared to pursue careers as professional actors in various media, equipped with a versatile skill set and a deep understanding of the acting profession.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, Federal, State, University funds

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: To apply as a first-year student, applicants must submit the Common Application and USC Writing Supplement (which includes a personal essay and USC-specific short answer questions), Official High School Transcripts, and two Letters of Recommendation (one from a school counselor and one from a teacher in a core academic subject). Submission of SAT or ACT scores is optional for Fall 2024 first-year applicants. Portfolios are only required for specific majors and are not required for Aerospace Engineering.
Department: Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering is offered by the Department of Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in engineering principles and prepares students to analyze, design, and operate aerospace systems. Course work includes an introduction to the different fields of aerospace engineering, such as aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, flight mechanics and orbital mechanics, and includes design projects that give students hands-on experience in aerospace system development. The curriculum also includes courses in mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer programming, materials science, electrical engineering, and manufacturing. The aerospace engineering curriculum prepares students for careers in the aerospace industry, government laboratories, and for graduate studies in aerospace engineering. The program also provides a good foundation for careers in other fields, such as automotive, energy, and biomedical engineering. The program prepares students to attain the following educational objectives: (1) Our graduates will establish themselves as successful engineers in industry, government, or other professional careers by demonstrating technical proficiency, communication skills, and responsible teamwork. (2) Our graduates will be able to engage in continued learning and professional development.
Accredidation: All undergraduate degree programs in engineering are accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, 111 Market Place, Suite 1050, Baltimore, MD 21202-4012; telephone 410-347-7700.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Popular Culture
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: This interdisciplinary program gives students an opportunity to explore the historical contexts, theoretical issues, critical methods, and cultural forms that constitute American popular culture. Through courses from a number of different departments, students are encouraged to consider popular culture in relation to high culture; to examine the specific qualities of various popular culture genres, forms, and media; to develop critical skills in analyzing popular culture; and to develop an understanding of popular culture’s role in shaping individual and social identities. The program provides an excellent foundation for careers in the entertainment and communications industries, public relations, arts management, teaching, and law, as well as for further graduate study in a variety of fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Medical Laboratory Science
Requirements: Submit the Common Application (including the USC Writing Supplement), official transcripts, the School Report and Counselor Recommendation, and one Teacher Recommendation (optional for Fall 2024, not needed for Spring 2025). SAT or ACT scores are optional for Fall 2025 applicants.
Department: Keck School of Medicine of USC
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Medical Laboratory Science (MLS) program prepares students for a career in the medical laboratory field. The program provides students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences and professional courses in clinical laboratory disciplines. Students gain expertise in performing diagnostic laboratory tests in areas such as clinical chemistry, hematology, immunology, microbiology, transfusion medicine, and molecular diagnostics. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and quality assurance in the clinical laboratory setting. Students will also learn about laboratory operations, management, and ethical responsibilities. The program includes extensive hands-on laboratory experience and supervised clinical rotations in affiliated hospitals and clinical laboratories. Graduates are prepared for entry-level positions as medical laboratory scientists in various healthcare settings, including hospitals, clinics, public health laboratories, and research facilities. Students who successfully complete the program are eligible to take national certification examinations in medical laboratory science.
Accredidation: The MLS program is accredited by the National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Sciences (NAACLS), 5600 N. River Rd., Suite 720, Rosemont, IL 60018-5119; (773) 714-8880.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Narrative Studies
Requirements: First-year applicants submit: Common Application with USC Writing Supplement, Transcripts, Letters of Recommendation, and Standardized Test Scores (optional for Fall 2023 & Fall 2024).
Department: Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

Requirements:
To apply to USC, you must submit the following items:
*   Common Application
*   USC Writing Supplement (part of the Common App)
    *   One 250-word short answer question
    *   Two 250-word short answer questions specific to USC
*   High School Transcript
*   Counselor Recommendation
*   Teacher Recommendation
*   Mid-Year Report (if available)
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Neuroscience (BS) program at USC is an interdepartmental program that provides a rigorous and broad education in neuroscience. Administered through the Neuroscience Graduate Program, the BS program combines strong foundations in biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics with a multidisciplinary understanding of brain function. Students are provided with hands-on research experience and opportunities to explore the various facets of neuroscience, from molecular and cellular mechanisms to systems and cognitive processes.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Public Policy
Requirements:
Your application consists of the following components:
*   Common Application with USC Writing Supplement
*   Counselor Recommendation (via Common Application)
*   Teacher Recommendation (via Common Application)
*   High School Transcript(s)
*   Mid-Year Grades (required for Regular Decision, optional for Early Action)
*   Test Scores (SAT or ACT) – optional for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025
*   School Report (via Common Application)

To be eligible for admission to USC, you must meet the following minimum requirements:
*   Graduate from an accredited high school or obtain a GED.
*   Complete 16 academic core subjects with a grade of C or better in all courses:
    *   4 years of English
    *   3 years of mathematics (Algebra I, Geometry, Algebra II)
    *   2 years of a laboratory science
    *   2 years of a foreign language (of the same language)
    *   1 year of visual or performing arts
    *   1 year of world history
    *   2 years of academic electives
Department: Sol Price School of Public Policy
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Public Policy is a multidisciplinary major that provides students with a strong foundation in political science, economics, policy analysis and quantitative methods. Students gain the analytical, communication, and leadership skills necessary to address complex societal challenges and make a positive impact through public service. The curriculum integrates theoretical knowledge with practical applications, preparing students for a variety of careers in government, non-profit organizations, and the private sector, as well as for graduate studies in public policy, law, and related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Quantitative Biology
Requirements: Applicants must submit the Common Application, USC Writing Supplement (including essays), Official Transcripts, School Report and Counselor Recommendation, and a Mid-Year Report. SAT or ACT scores are optional.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences and USC Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Quantitative Biology program is designed for students interested in combining a strong foundation in biology with a rigorous training in mathematics, statistics, computer science, and data analysis. The curriculum provides students with the quantitative skills necessary to address complex biological problems, from molecular to ecological scales. Graduates will be prepared for careers in research, biotechnology, computational biology, and further graduate studies in quantitative biology, bioinformatics, biostatistics, and related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Real Estate Development
Requirements:
Application Requirements for First-Year Students:
*   Common Application
*   USC Writing Supplement
*   Official high school transcripts
*   SAT or ACT scores (optional for 2024-2025)
*   Letters of Recommendation (optional)
Department: USC Price School of Public Policy
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Real Estate Development is a four-year professional degree program designed for students seeking to enter the field of real estate development. The undergraduate curriculum provides a strong background in the analytical and practical skills necessary to perform as a real estate development professional. The program encompasses both the private sector market-driven activities of property development, finance and management, and the public sector concerns for quality urban environments, economic development, community planning and infrastructure development. The curriculum provides a foundation in critical thinking, writing and oral presentation skills, as well as a solid understanding of market and economic analysis, regulatory review, finance, accounting and investment. Elective opportunities provide the student with flexibility in pursuing a particular area of interest in real estate development.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Spatial Sciences
Requirements: The Common Application or Coalition Application, including the USC Writing Supplement with two required essays, official high school transcripts, and letter(s) of recommendation (one required). Standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional.
Department: Spatial Sciences Institute
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Spatial Sciences (BA) offers students the opportunity to integrate an understanding of how spatial analysis and visualization technologies contribute to the creation of new knowledge in diverse fields of inquiry with a firm grounding in the liberal arts tradition. The curriculum provides core knowledge and skills in geographic information science and spatial data analysis, geographic information systems, remote sensing, and geodesy necessary for students to analyze complex geospatial data and derive meaningful information. Students may choose to use these core skills for an academic emphasis in either natural science or social science, complementing other course work in traditional disciplines such as geology, environmental studies, archaeology, political science, sociology, economics, or public policy. The BA in Spatial Sciences is an appropriate degree for students who want a grounding in spatial methods but intend to apply them as an integral part of another field of study such as international relations, journalism, urban planning, or business. This program may also be a good choice for students interested in graduate studies in a related field such as urban planning, public policy, public health, landscape architecture, business administration, political science, or communications. Students in the BA in Spatial Sciences are strongly encouraged to consider a minor or a second major in an area of their disciplinary interest.
ScholarshipType: Freshman Scholarships, Transfer Scholarships, Current Student Scholarships, External Scholarships

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Spatial Sciences
Requirements: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, High School Transcript, SAT or ACT Scores (Optional for 2024 and 2025 Applicants), Portfolio, SlideRoom, or Audition (if applicable), Mid-Year Grades (if applicable), TOEFL, IELTS, PTE Academic or Duolingo English Test Scores (if applicable)
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Spatial Sciences offers a comprehensive foundation in spatial theory, methods, and applications. Students develop expertise in geographic information science and technology (GIS&T) and gain practical skills in data acquisition, management, analysis, visualization, and communication, including experience with cutting-edge spatial software, big data, artificial intelligence, and virtual and augmented reality applications. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and ethical considerations related to spatial data. Graduates are prepared for diverse careers in fields such as environmental science, urban planning, public health, business, and national security, or for further graduate studies.

Department: USC School of Dramatic Arts
Concentration: Emphasis in Design, Emphasis in Stage Management
Description: The BA in Theatre program offers a broad-based, liberal arts approach to the study of theatre. Designed for students who wish to pursue a major in theatre within the context of a strong general education, the program encourages students to develop skills in various aspects of theatre, including performance, dramatic literature, history, theory, and design. The program encourages students to explore multiple facets of theatre and potentially combine their studies with a minor or second major in another field. The program prepares students for a wide range of careers in the arts and other fields that value creative problem-solving, critical thinking, and collaborative skills.

Requirements: Applicants must submit the Common Application (including essays), USC Writing Supplement (including essays and short answer questions), official high school transcripts, school report and counselor recommendation, mid-year school report (if applicable), and final school report (if applicable). Optional materials include a resume and portfolio. Applicants to all undergraduate programs at USC Dornsife apply through the USC Office of Admission.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor in Adult Development, Gerontology, and Aging
Department: Leonard Davis School of Gerontology
Description: The Bachelor in Adult Development, Gerontology, and Aging is designed for students who want to develop an understanding of the aging process from a multidisciplinary perspective. The program emphasizes both biological and social science approaches to the study of adult development and aging. Students in this program will learn about the social, psychological, biological, and economic aspects of aging, and how these factors impact individuals and society. The curriculum prepares students for careers in gerontology and related fields, such as health care, social services, public policy, and research. It also provides a strong foundation for graduate studies in gerontology or other related disciplines.

Requirements: Applying to USC as a first-year undergraduate applicant involves submitting the Common Application, including essays. Other required documents include Official Transcripts, a School Report, a Mid-Year Report, and an academic Letter of Recommendation. Submission of SAT or ACT test scores is optional for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 applicants.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The major in African American Studies provides an interdisciplinary approach to the study of people of African descent in the Americas and their global impact, with a particular focus on the United States and the Black Atlantic. This major introduces students to the theories and methods of the study of race and ethnicity, and trains them to engage critically in the analysis of power, inequality, and resistance. Coursework enables students to develop strong research, analytical, and communication skills, which are essential for careers in diverse fields, including education, public policy, community organizing, public health, social work, law, journalism, communications, and the arts.

Requirements: First-Year applicants apply to USC through the USC Undergraduate Admission office, not directly to the department. General application requirements for first-year students include the Common Application (which includes essays and activities list), the USC Writing Supplement (which includes additional short answer questions), and official high school transcripts. Letter(s) of Recommendation are optional. SAT or ACT scores are optional. Portfolio, slide room, or other creative samples are required if applicable to the student's application.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: Anthropology is the comparative study of human biological and cultural diversity across space and time. Anthropologists examine human origins and evolution, how humans adapt to different environments, and how they create meaning through language, art, ritual, and religion. Our undergraduate curriculum in Anthropology provides a comprehensive introduction to all four subfields of anthropology – sociocultural anthropology, linguistic anthropology, archaeological anthropology, and biological anthropology – with a particular emphasis on theoretical issues and the role of ethnographic, archaeological, and biological fieldwork. The Anthropology program prepares students for a wide range of careers. The major will give students an excellent foundation in human diversity and cross-cultural understanding, valuable for today’s globalized world. Many students choose to pursue graduate studies in Anthropology (cultural, biological, and archaeology), Public Health, Medical Anthropology, Law, International Relations, Education, or Journalism. Other students use their degrees to begin careers in government, non-profits, museums, international NGOs, forensic science, advertising, marketing, public relations, and business, or to enter the health professions. Our unique curriculum combines intellectual rigor with flexibility, allowing students to tailor their programs according to their interests while providing them with the necessary skills to be successful.
