Requirements: First-Year Application Checklist: Common App or Coalition App, USC Writing Supplement, Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, Official High School Transcripts, School Report, Mid-Year Report (if applicable). Optional materials include SAT/ACT Scores and a Resume. Portfolio, Audition, or Interview are optional for specific majors.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The archaeology program provides undergraduates with the opportunity to study the past through its material remains and learn methods and theories that are broadly applicable to a range of fields that examine human culture and society. Students develop an understanding of major themes in the history of human societies around the globe from the earliest origins to the present. The major offers students a broad, cross-cultural, and humanistic understanding of the past through the study of material culture, supplemented by training in the methods and theories of archaeological field and laboratory work. The major also emphasizes developing critical thinking and analytical skills, as well as an appreciation of the social and ethical responsibilities of those who study the past and its remains. The program offers opportunities for students to participate in archaeological fieldwork and laboratory work through faculty-led projects in the Los Angeles area and abroad. Many of our students are also interested in careers in heritage management and cultural resource management. Students can undertake internships in museums, historical societies, government agencies and private firms. The department has close ties with museums and cultural heritage institutions in the Los Angeles area, including the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County, the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, and the J. Paul Getty Museum.

Requirements: First-Year Applicants must submit the Common Application with the USC Writing Supplement. Transfer Applicants must submit the Common Application with the USC Writing Supplement. The Common Application asks for a personal essay and for your academic record including a list of courses and grades achieved, and scores on standardized tests (SAT/ACT). The USC Writing Supplement asks for short answers and additional essays. All applicants to the Bachelor of Architecture program are required to submit a portfolio.
Department: USC School of Architecture
Description: The Bachelor in Architecture is a five-year professional degree program that integrates general education with a comprehensive curriculum in architectural design, history, theory, building technology, and professional practice. The curriculum emphasizes the development of strong conceptual design abilities and a comprehensive understanding of the cultural, historical, and technological issues of architecture. This program provides students with the intellectual and creative skills to address the complex challenges of the built environment and prepares them for professional careers in architecture and related fields. Students gain a broad understanding of the various aspects of architectural practice, including project management, professional ethics, and client relations, ensuring they are well-prepared for entry into the architectural profession.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Architecture is accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB).

Requirements: All first-year applicants must submit the following: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement (includes one long essay and two short answer questions), Official high school transcripts, Mid-year senior year grades, Letters of recommendation (at least one from a counselor or teacher, up to two), SAT or ACT scores (optional).
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: Art History majors choose from a wide variety of courses, examining art, architecture, and visual culture from across the globe and throughout history. Through courses that span ancient to contemporary periods and a diverse array of media, students gain an understanding of the historical production, critical reception, and evolving theories of visual art. The curriculum introduces students to a range of methodologies, equipping them with a robust toolkit for analyzing and interpreting images and objects. As a result, Art History majors cultivate their skills in critical thinking, visual analysis, and written and oral communication, preparing them for a range of professional fields. These skills are further strengthened by experiential learning opportunities, including internships at museums and galleries and study abroad programs, which allow students to encounter art firsthand and deepen their knowledge of visual culture. The BA in Art History provides a flexible, interdisciplinary education that fosters intellectual curiosity and prepares students for diverse career paths in the arts and beyond, from graduate study in art history or related fields, to work in museums, galleries, auction houses, non-profit arts organizations, publishing, conservation, historic preservation, teaching, and arts administration.

Requirements: Required Application Components: Common Application or Coalition Application, USC Writing Supplement, High school transcript(s), SAT or ACT scores (Optional for Fall 2024, 2025, 2026 applicants), Portfolio, slide room, or audition, if applicable. Not Required, but Considered: Letters of Recommendation, Interviews. Other Requirements: English Proficiency (if applicable), Financial Aid Application.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

Requirements: Common App with USC Supplement, High school transcript(s), Letter(s) of recommendation (one counselor, one teacher), Essays (short answers + one longer essay required on Common App), English Proficiency (for international students). Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are not required for Fall 2024 applicants; students may choose to submit them, but will not be disadvantaged if they do not.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

Requirements: First-year applicants must submit the following application materials: Official High School Transcripts; SAT/ACT Scores (Optional for 2024); Letters of Recommendation; Essays; Portfolio, Audition, and/or Interview (for some majors); English Proficiency (International Applicants Only).
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The universe is presented in terms of astrophysical principles that govern the evolution and structure of planets, stars, galaxies and the universe as a whole. Both observational and theoretical approaches are explored. Courses for non-science majors emphasize the cultural and historical impact of astronomy, as well as the scientific context of current discoveries. Majors in astronomy and astrophysics combine courses in physics and astronomy with an emphasis on research. The program also offers students the opportunity to learn modern astronomical research techniques using the telescopes at the Mount Wilson Observatory.

Department: Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Astronautical Engineering program provides a strong foundation in the fundamental engineering disciplines of mathematics, physics, chemistry, materials science, statics, dynamics, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, and electrical circuits. Emphasis is placed on the scientific and technological foundations of modern astronautics. The program also provides a basic understanding of aerodynamics, orbital mechanics, spacecraft dynamics and control, rocket propulsion, and space environment. Laboratory experience is included in the curriculum. All students are required to take a set of core courses and then complete additional units in the areas of astronautics and aerospace electives.

Requirements: General application requirements at USC typically include official academic transcripts, letters of recommendation (e.g., from a counselor and teacher for first-year applicants, or academic/professional recommenders for graduate applicants), and written components such as essays/writing supplements for undergraduate applicants or a Statement of Purpose for graduate applicants. Undergraduate applicants provide an activities list via the Common Application, while graduate applicants generally submit a CV/Resume. Standardized test scores, such as SAT/ACT for undergraduates or GRE/GMAT/TOEFL/IELTS for graduates, may also be part of the application, often as an optional component for undergraduates.

First-Year applicants must submit: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, Official Transcripts, Counselor Recommendation, and Teacher Recommendation. Standardized Test Scores (SAT/ACT) are optional for students applying for the Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 semesters.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The undergraduate program in biochemistry is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the chemical and biological sciences. The interdisciplinary nature of biochemistry requires students to become proficient in many scientific fields and to integrate this knowledge to solve problems at the interface of chemistry and biology. This preparation provides a foundation for careers in research, medicine and other health professions, biotechnology, and many other fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
Requirements: Common Application; USC Writing Supplement; Official high school transcripts; SAT or ACT scores (optional for Fall 2024, Fall 2025, and Fall 2026 applicants); Letters of recommendation; School Report; Mid-Year Report.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology provides students with a strong background in the chemistry and biology of living systems. The curriculum offers substantial training in chemistry, mathematics, physics and biology, and then focuses on the molecular aspects of biochemistry and molecular biology. The program is designed to provide excellent preparation for students interested in graduate studies in these and related fields as well as careers in medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, biotechnology, and many other health-related fields. In addition to a rigorous academic curriculum, the program offers opportunities to engage in cutting-edge research in a wide range of fields from structural biology to genomics.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Bioengineering and Biomedical Engineering
Department: Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: Biomedical engineering is a field dedicated to the application of engineering principles and design concepts to medicine and biology. This field seeks to close the gap between engineering and medicine, combining the design and problem-solving skills of engineering with medical and biological sciences to advance health care treatment, including diagnosis, monitoring, and therapy. The undergraduate curriculum provides a strong foundation in physical, chemical, and biological sciences and mathematics, an introduction to basic engineering principles and design, and a comprehensive exposure to the breadth of biomedical engineering. Through its curriculum, the program prepares students for careers in medical device, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and health care industries, as well as for further graduate studies in biomedical engineering or other professional programs, such as medicine and law.

Requirements: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, Mid-Year Report (if applicable), Official Transcripts, Standardized Test Scores (optional for Fall 2024 applicants), Portfolio (required for some arts majors)
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

Requirements: Applicants are generally required to submit an online application and official transcripts from all previously attended academic institutions. For undergraduate applicants, this includes the Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, high school transcripts, counselor and teacher recommendations, and a mid-year report. Standardized test scores (ACT/SAT) are optional for undergraduate applicants through Fall 2026. For graduate applicants, general requirements include an online application, transcripts, a statement of purpose, and often letters of recommendation. Standardized tests (e.g., GRE, GMAT, TOEFL, IELTS) may be required for graduate applicants depending on the specific program.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

Requirements: Applicants must submit the Common Application (including the USC Writing Supplement), counselor recommendation, teacher recommendation, official high school transcripts, and the application fee or fee waiver. A mid-year school report is required if applicable. SAT or ACT scores are optional for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 applicants.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Global Biotechnology program is an interdisciplinary program that draws faculty from across the university in areas of biology, chemistry, engineering, and business. The program offers students an opportunity to learn about the science, business, and regulatory aspects of biotechnology with emphasis on their global implications. The curriculum includes foundation courses in life sciences and chemistry, advanced courses in biotechnology, and electives covering various aspects of science, business, and policy. Students will be prepared for careers in the biotechnology industry, government, non-profit organizations, or for further graduate studies.

Requirements: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, Official High School Transcripts, Letter(s) of Recommendation (optional), SAT or ACT scores (optional for Fall 2024, 2025, and 2026 applicants), Portfolio, slide room submission, or audition (required for some specific majors).
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

Requirements: Common App or Coalition Application, USC Writing Supplement, Official High School Transcripts, Mid-Year Report, Letters of Recommendation (from counselor and teacher), Test Scores (SAT or ACT) – optional for Fall 2024, Fall 2025, and Fall 2026 applicants.
Department: Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: Chemical engineers are concerned with the application of chemical principles to the solution of practical problems. Their work requires an understanding of chemical and physical principles and is unique in its emphasis on process design, particularly involving the transformation of materials. They are responsible for the design and operation of processes for the manufacture of products as diverse as rocket propellants, computer chips, pharmaceuticals, synthetic fibers, plastics, petroleum products, processed foods and beverages, and basic chemicals for industry. The chemical engineer also plays a vital role in medical applications, environmental protection and new materials development. Undergraduate instruction is designed to give the student a strong foundation in chemistry, physics and mathematics and to integrate this material into the engineering sciences through the core chemical engineering courses. The department offers the Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, www.abet.org.

Department: COLLEGE OF LETTERS, ARTS AND SCIENCES
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in chemistry is the appropriate course of study for students contemplating a career in chemistry or a related field (such as biochemistry, chemical physics or materials science), or for students intending to pursue graduate work in chemistry. This degree meets the certification standards of the American Chemical Society.
Accredidation: Meets the certification standards of the American Chemical Society.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Cinematography and Video Production
Requirements: First-year applicants must complete the Common Application or Coalition Application, the USC Writing Supplement, and official high school transcripts. Applicants to the USC School of Cinematic Arts are strongly encouraged to submit one letter of recommendation from an academic source and one from a cinematic arts source. SAT or ACT scores are NOT required for applicants applying for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025. A portfolio is required for all Cinematic Arts applicants, submitted via the USC Cinematic Arts portal. For Bachelor in Cinematography and Video Production (B.F.A.) applicants, the portfolio must include: a Creative Sample (a one-page written proposal for a short film, video, or animation you would like to direct, including title, log line, genre, description of story, style, visual approach, and specific interest in the project); a Visual Sample (12-15 original photographs demonstrating your visual aesthetic in JPG format, do NOT submit any video); and Short Response Questions. International applicants may also be required to submit TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE Academic scores.
Department: School of Cinematic Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Film and Television Production program offers intensive professional training in the cinematic arts combined with a thorough general education. BFA students apply for admission to the program directly from high school. The program provides the conceptual and technical skills necessary for success in the rapidly evolving media environment. Students select one of seven areas of study in which to specialize: producing, writing, directing, cinematography, editing, sound, or animation and digital arts. Students gain a deeper knowledge of the history, theory and aesthetics of moving images. Through a variety of required courses in the liberal arts, students also broaden their understanding of the world, developing the critical thinking skills, humanistic perspective and global awareness necessary for creative expression.

Requirements: A complete application includes: The Common Application or Coalition Application, powered by Scoir, USC Writing Supplement, Official transcripts, and Test scores (SAT or ACT) are optional. Letters of Recommendation are not required for first-year applicants for fall 2024.
Department: Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: Civil engineering is a professional engineering discipline that deals with the design, construction, and maintenance of the physical and naturally built environment, including public works such as roads, bridges, canals, dams, airports, sewerage systems, pipelines, structural components of buildings, and railways. At USC, we offer a comprehensive Bachelor of Science (BS) program in Civil Engineering that prepares students for careers in various fields, including structural, geotechnical, water resources, environmental, transportation, and construction engineering. Our curriculum provides a strong foundation in engineering principles, mathematics, and science, combined with hands-on experience through laboratory work, field trips, and design projects. Our program emphasizes sustainability, resilience, and ethical considerations, preparing graduates to address complex challenges facing society, such as climate change, urbanization, and infrastructure development. With a focus on innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration, our students gain the skills and knowledge necessary to contribute to the advancement of civil engineering and make a positive impact on the world.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science program in Civil Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Concentration: Ancient History; Classical Culture; Classical Languages and Literature
Description: The Department of Classics offers a Bachelor of Arts degree in Classics. The major is designed to provide students with a broad and flexible education based on the languages and cultures of ancient Greece and Rome, and their lasting influence. It offers three areas of emphasis: Ancient History, Classical Culture, and Classical Languages and Literature. Students are encouraged to consult with the undergraduate advisor in Classics to determine which area of emphasis best suits their interests and professional goals. The major in Classics offers a comprehensive study of the civilizations of Greece and Rome, including their literature, history, philosophy, art, and archaeology. It is designed to provide students with a broad and flexible education based on the languages and cultures of ancient Greece and Rome, and their lasting influence. Students develop critical thinking, analytical, and communication skills applicable to a wide range of careers and graduate studies.

Requirements: Students applying to USC must use the Common Application. Application materials should be submitted online at commonapp.org. Official transcripts from all secondary schools attended. We require one letter of recommendation from either your high school counselor or a teacher. We also accept additional letters of recommendation from others who know you well and can speak to your strengths. The Common Application includes a main essay and additional questions specific to USC. We seek to understand the intellectual curiosity and academic interests of our applicants, as well as their involvement in community and extracurricular activities. USC is test-optional for students applying for fall 2024. If you opt to submit test scores, we will accept either the SAT or ACT.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Cognitive Science major is designed for students interested in the scientific study of the mind, brain and intelligent systems. It provides students with an interdisciplinary understanding of the nature of intelligence through the perspectives and methodologies of psychology, computer science, linguistics and philosophy. Students will explore topics such as perception, memory, reasoning, language, decision-making, artificial intelligence and the neural basis of cognition. The program emphasizes critical thinking, research skills and the integration of knowledge from diverse fields. The curriculum offers a solid foundation in the core areas of cognitive science, along with opportunities for specialization through elective courses.
ScholarshipType: Federal, State, Institutional, Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, ROTC

Requirements: Applicants must submit the Common App application and USC Writing Supplement, official high school transcripts, one letter of recommendation, and a Common App personal essay. SAT or ACT scores are optional for the 2024 and 2025 application cycles. The USC Annenberg School of Communication and Journalism does not have additional supplemental application requirements for first-year students.
Department: USC Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
Description: Communication is arguably the most vital skill in modern society. In a world of digital transformation, social change and global challenges, the need for effective and ethical communicators continues to grow exponentially. The USC Annenberg Bachelor of Arts in Communication program develops students into communication leaders and innovative thinkers, capable of leveraging communication for good and for success across a variety of professional industries and sectors. Annenberg communication majors master foundational theories while also gaining exposure to a diverse range of subject matters relevant to contemporary communication contexts including: health communication, intercultural communication, political communication, organizational communication, social media, entertainment and persuasive communication. Students develop rigorous research skills to analyze complex issues and formulate strategies that impact individuals, institutions, and society at large. Our graduates enter the workforce equipped with the ability to think critically, communicate effectively across multiple platforms, and engage ethically with diverse communities.

Department: COLLEGE OF LETTERS, ARTS AND SCIENCES
Description: Comparative Literature is an interdisciplinary field that investigates literature and culture across national, linguistic, and disciplinary boundaries. The undergraduate major introduces students to global literary traditions, critical methodologies, and translation studies, offering a rigorous humanities education and excellent preparation for graduate study in any humanities discipline or for careers in a wide range of fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Computational and Applied Mathematics
Requirements: Required items: Common Application (includes a personal essay and space to list your activities and achievements), USC Writing Supplement, Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, School Report, Transcripts, Mid-Year Report (if available). Optional items: Standardized Test Scores (SAT/ACT). USC is test-optional for students applying for undergraduate admission for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: This degree emphasizes the modern role of mathematics in the sciences, engineering, and data analysis. Students develop a strong analytical foundation and gain extensive experience with advanced mathematical and computational techniques required to solve problems in scientific and engineering disciplines. Students interested in this degree program should apply to the Bachelor of Science in Applied and Computational Mathematics major. For more information, please refer to the USC Catalogue.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Computer and Information Sciences
Requirements: All applicants must submit: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, Official high school transcripts. Letters of recommendation and SAT or ACT scores are optional for Fall 2024 applicants. International students may also need to submit official test scores for English proficiency and a financial statement.
Department: USC Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: The Bachelor in Computer and Information Sciences program is designed to provide students with a broad and rigorous foundation in the theoretical and applied aspects of computer science and information systems. Graduates will be prepared for careers in various computing fields, further graduate studies, and lifelong learning. Upon completion of the Bachelor in Computer and Information Sciences program, students will be able to: Apply fundamental concepts of computer science, including algorithms, data structures, and programming paradigms, to solve complex problems. Design, implement, and evaluate software systems that meet specified requirements. Analyze and interpret data to support decision-making processes. Understand ethical and professional responsibilities in the computing profession. Communicate effectively in technical and non-technical contexts.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, specific criteria (e.g., academic achievement, special talent, leadership, community service, or financial need)

Department: School of Cinematic Arts
Description: The Bachelor in Computer Graphics is an interdisciplinary program that emphasizes an advanced knowledge of the aesthetics and practice of computer graphics as they apply to film, television, games, advertising, and scientific visualization. This program will be housed within the Interactive Media and Games Division of the School of Cinematic Arts, in conjunction with the Computer Science Department in the Viterbi School of Engineering. Students are trained for creative, technical, and management positions. This degree offers a common foundation in both areas, combining computer graphics courses with core courses in computer science. Graduates will possess strong artistic and technical skills. They will be prepared to pursue careers across a wide range of industries including visual effects, games, animation, VR/AR, and more.

Department: Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: A bachelor’s degree in computer hardware engineering covers all aspects of modern computer systems. Students learn how to design, build, and test computer hardware, including microprocessors, memory, and peripherals. They also gain a deep understanding of computer architecture, operating systems, and software development. The curriculum includes courses in digital logic design, computer organization, embedded systems, and very large-scale integration (VLSI) design. Graduates are prepared for careers in hardware design, development, and testing, as well as for graduate studies in computer engineering or related fields.

Requirements: Applicants must submit the Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, official high school transcripts, and a Letter of Recommendation. SAT or ACT scores are optional for Fall 2024 applicants.
Department: Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in Computer Science is designed to prepare students for careers in the computing industry or for graduate study. This program provides a strong foundation in the theoretical and algorithmic foundations of computer science, as well as hands-on experience in software development. Students gain proficiency in programming languages, data structures, algorithms, operating systems, computer architecture, and software engineering principles. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and innovative design, enabling students to tackle complex computational challenges. Students have the option of pursuing a general computer science curriculum or specializing in various areas through elective courses. The program also provides opportunities for research, internships, and capstone projects, preparing graduates for diverse roles in fields such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, cybersecurity, game development, and more.

Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in English offers students an opportunity to study the English literary tradition and its relation to other literary and cultural traditions, as well as the history, theory, and practice of rhetoric and composition. The program provides a foundation in literary history, critical theory, and interdisciplinary approaches to culture. Students learn to read carefully, think critically, and write clearly and persuasively. The Creative Writing Emphasis allows students to gain extensive practice in writing and revising their own fiction, poetry, or nonfiction. Students complete a total of three creative writing workshops and produce a significant portfolio of work in their chosen genre.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, Artistic talent, Leadership, Departmental awards, National Merit

Department: USC Glorya Kaufman School of Dance
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Dance degree is a four-year, conservatory-style, pre-professional program that fully immerses students in the theory and practice of dance. Through a holistic and rigorous curriculum, students are challenged to explore their artistic, intellectual and creative potential, while gaining an understanding of the historical, theoretical and scientific foundations of the field. Emphasis is placed on developing a comprehensive skill set in ballet, contemporary and hip-hop techniques, improvisation, choreography, performance, dance science and somatic practices. The program culminates in a senior-year capstone project that allows students to integrate their accumulated knowledge and skills to create a final artistic statement. This degree prepares students for professional careers as dancers, choreographers, educators, arts administrators and scholars, as well as for graduate study in dance and related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Design and Visual Communications
Requirements: To apply to the Bachelor in Design and Visual Communications program at USC Roski School of Art and Design, applicants must submit the following: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, USC Roski SlideRoom Portfolio, Official high school transcripts and school records, Letter of Recommendation (from a counselor or a teacher), SAT or ACT scores (optional for fall 2024 applicants), English proficiency examination scores (required for international students).
Department: Roski School of Art and Design
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in Design and Visual Communications is designed to provide students with a broad and interdisciplinary understanding of the theory, history, and practice of design and visual communication. The program integrates various approaches to visual communication, including graphic design, illustration, photography, and new media, within a liberal arts framework. Students will develop critical thinking skills, visual literacy, and practical design abilities, preparing them for careers in fields such as graphic design, advertising, web design, multimedia, and art direction, or for further graduate study.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Drama and Theatre Production
Requirements: Applicants must complete the University of Southern California (USC) application via the Common Application, and a supplemental application to the USC School of Dramatic Arts (SDA) via SlideRoom. The Common Application requires essays (including the USC Writing Supplement), letters of recommendation from a counselor and teacher, and high school transcripts. Standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional for Fall 2024 first-year applicants. The SDA SlideRoom application requires a headshot, a theatrical resume, a Statement of Purpose (essay) indicating why the applicant wishes to attend the USC School of Dramatic Arts, and two additional letters of recommendation. An interview with faculty is required for this program.
Department: USC School of Dramatic Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Drama and Theatre Production is offered by the School of Dramatic Arts. The program gives students a comprehensive liberal arts education within the context of a focused theatre curriculum, enabling them to understand the nature of theatrical experience and the creative process, as well as to develop their own artistic abilities and professional skills. Students completing the degree will demonstrate a broad knowledge of theatre and its literature, history and theory; communicate an understanding of the relationship between their craft and other art forms; and articulate the importance of theatre to society and culture. The program provides the basic theatre production curriculum found in the BFA programs at USC, but within the broader liberal arts foundation of a BA degree.

Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Earth Sciences is designed for students seeking a strong foundation in geological sciences and preparing for professional careers or graduate studies. The Earth Sciences curriculum offers a wide range of courses in areas such as geology, geophysics, oceanography, paleontology, geochemistry and environmental science. Opportunities exist for individual research with a faculty member. The program has strong ties to the Earth Sciences department, which supports a wide array of research covering modern and ancient processes that shape Earth, other planets, and their environments. The rigorous scientific curriculum, coupled with computational skills, prepares students for advanced studies or careers in fields such as environmental consulting, natural resource management, geological surveying, and risk assessment.

ProgramName: Bachelor in East Asian Area Studies
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The East Asian Area Studies program provides students with a broad interdisciplinary exposure to the cultures and societies of East Asia (China, Japan, and Korea). The curriculum integrates the study of East Asian languages with study in the humanities and social sciences. The program emphasizes both breadth and depth within the East Asian area, and provides a solid base for students who wish to pursue graduate work or careers in teaching, journalism, business, law, or government service involving East Asia. Courses in the program combine work in East Asian languages with courses in anthropology, art history, comparative literature, economics, geography, history, international relations, philosophy, political science, religion, and sociology. A regional emphasis (China, Japan, or Korea) is normally selected by the student.

ProgramName: Bachelor in East Asian Languages and Cultures
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The East Asian Languages and Cultures program is designed for students who desire to gain a deep knowledge of the cultures of East Asia, past and present. It offers the student flexibility in selecting courses that reflect individual interests and goals, while also ensuring exposure to a broad range of knowledge across the various disciplines that constitute the field of East Asian studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor in East Asian Languages and Literatures
Requirements: First-Year Applicant Checklist: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, Official High School Transcripts, SAT or ACT Scores (Optional for Fall 2024, Fall 2025, and Fall 2026), Portfolio, Audition, or Interview (If Required by Major), Mid-Year Grades (For First-Year Applicants)
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures offers a Bachelor of Arts degree in East Asian Languages and Literatures. This major is designed to provide students with comprehensive training in an East Asian language and a broad knowledge of East Asian literary and cultural traditions. Students may concentrate in Chinese, Japanese or Korean. The major combines intensive language study with a sequence of courses on East Asian literature and culture designed to develop critical thinking skills and cultural competency. With their knowledge of an East Asian language and culture, graduates are well prepared for careers in fields such as business, law, international relations, teaching, and translation. The major also provides a strong foundation for advanced graduate study in East Asian languages and cultures.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
Requirements: Required materials vary depending on the applicant's academic history and major of interest. See additional requirements listed for first-year and transfer applicants. Required materials may include: Online Application (Common Application or Coalition Application), Official Transcripts, School Report, Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, Mid-Year Report. A personal essay is required of all applicants.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology is the study of interactions among organisms and between organisms and their environment (ecology), and the origins and processes of change in biodiversity over time (evolutionary biology). The Bachelor of Science degree in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology provides students with rigorous training in the fundamentals of ecology, evolutionary biology, and organismal biology, and allows students to specialize in areas of particular interest to them. This program prepares students for graduate studies in ecology, evolution, and organismal biology, and for careers in ecological consulting, conservation, environmental law and policy, and science education. The department provides students with opportunities to participate in original research with faculty, both on campus and at the Wrigley Marine Science Center on Catalina Island.

Requirements: First-year applicants must submit the Common Application, including the USC Writing Supplement. Official high school transcripts are required. A letter of recommendation is optional. SAT or ACT scores are optional for Fall 2024, Fall 2025, and Fall 2026 applicants. English proficiency is required for international applicants whose native language is not English. Portfolios are required for specific majors only (Architecture, Art, Cinematic Arts, Dance, Music, Theatre).
Department: Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The department offers a Bachelor of Arts in Economics and two minors, a Minor in Economics and a Minor in Applied Analytics. All three programs provide an in-depth understanding of the principles and applications of economic analysis. Students learn how to analyze economic problems, evaluate policy proposals, and make informed decisions in a variety of contexts, from business to government to international relations. They also develop strong analytical, quantitative and communication skills that are highly valued in the job market and in graduate studies. Students can tailor their program to their interests and career goals by choosing from a wide range of elective courses in various fields of economics, such as behavioral economics, development economics, environmental economics, international economics, public economics and urban economics.

Requirements: Required Materials: Common Application (including USC-specific questions), Counselor Recommendation (via Common Application), Teacher Recommendation (via Common Application), Official High School Transcripts, Mid-Year Grades. Optional: SAT or ACT scores, Portfolio, Audition, or Interview (for specific majors). Academic Preparation: USC looks for students who have challenged themselves with a strong academic program. Our most competitive applicants are taking the most rigorous curriculum available to them, including AP, IB, and honors classes. Most successful applicants will have taken: 4 years of English, 3-4 years of mathematics (including Algebra I, Geometry, Algebra II, and Advanced Math), 3-4 years of laboratory science, 2-4 years of a foreign language, 2 years of history/social science.
Department: USC Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering (BS ECE) program at USC is a four-year curriculum administered by the Ming Hsieh Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. It is ideal for students who wish to pursue a rigorous, accredited program in electrical engineering with the flexibility to specialize in numerous areas ranging from classical electrical engineering to computer engineering to emerging areas in AI, machine learning and quantum computing. The BS ECE curriculum provides a strong foundation in core electrical and computer engineering principles, including circuit analysis, digital systems, electromagnetics, signals and systems, and programming. As you progress, you’ll have the flexibility to choose technical electives and pursue specializations that align with your interests and career goals.
Accredidation: Accredited by ABET (Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology).

Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: English majors at USC study a wide range of literatures in English, from the earliest periods to the most contemporary, with a strong focus on literary history and criticism. The program helps students develop skills in critical reading, analytical thinking, and persuasive writing. Graduates are well-prepared for careers in law, education, journalism, publishing, business, and public service, and for graduate studies in a variety of fields.

Requirements: All first-year applicants must complete the Common Application, which includes the Personal Essay, and the USC Writing Supplement. Additional requirements include a counselor recommendation, teacher recommendation, mid-year report, and official high school transcripts. Standardized Test Scores (SAT/ACT) are optional for Fall 2024, 2025 and 2026 applicants. Portfolios are optional for some majors.
Department: Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: The Environmental Engineering (BS) curriculum provides students with a strong foundation in science and engineering fundamentals. The program emphasizes the understanding and design of systems that protect and improve environmental quality for human health and ecological systems. The curriculum prepares students for careers in environmental protection and remediation; air pollution control; water and wastewater treatment; hazardous waste management; water resource management; environmental health; and climate change. Students are trained to identify and solve complex environmental problems using engineering principles and tools, as well as to develop sustainable solutions to protect natural resources and human well-being. The curriculum includes significant laboratory and design components. Students are encouraged to participate in research with faculty in areas such as air quality engineering, water quality engineering, solid and hazardous waste management, environmental biotechnology, and sustainable infrastructure.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, www.abet.org

Requirements: Common Application with USC Writing Supplement; Official High School Transcripts; Letters of Recommendation (optional); Standardized Test Scores (optional for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 applicants); Portfolio, Audition, or Interview (for certain majors only); English Proficiency (for international students only); Application Fee or Fee Waiver
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary field that seeks to understand the natural world and how human activities interact with and affect the environment. The Environmental Science program at USC provides students with a strong scientific foundation, critical thinking skills, and practical experience to address complex environmental challenges. Students will learn to analyze environmental problems from multiple perspectives, design and conduct scientific investigations, interpret data, and develop solutions. The curriculum covers a broad range of topics including ecology, geology, hydrology, atmospheric science, environmental chemistry, environmental policy, and sustainability. Graduates are prepared for careers in environmental consulting, government agencies, non-profit organizations, research institutions, and for graduate studies in environmental science and related fields.

Requirements: First-year applicants must submit the Common Application (including essays and short answer questions), official high school transcripts, a school report (counselor recommendation), and one teacher recommendation (two recommended). SAT/ACT scores are optional for Spring 2024 and Fall 2024 applicants.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Studies provides a liberal arts approach to the environment. The program is designed for students seeking a broad-based, interdisciplinary understanding of environmental issues, and prepares them for further study in areas such as environmental policy, law, or planning, or for careers in the private and non-profit sectors. Students learn to critically evaluate environmental problems, understand the scientific basis for environmental issues, and develop solutions from social, economic, political and ethical perspectives. The program emphasizes both quantitative and qualitative methods, providing students with a comprehensive skill set for addressing complex environmental challenges. Students are encouraged to develop an area of specialization through elective courses and research opportunities tailored to their individual interests. This major requires a significant number of courses in the natural sciences, social sciences, and humanities, and culminates in a senior capstone experience.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Film and Video Studies
Department: School of Cinematic Arts

ProgramName: Bachelor in French Language and Literature
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission to USC, first-year applicants must submit: the Common Application, which includes the Common Application Personal Essay; the USC Writing Supplement, which includes short answer questions and essays specific to USC; official transcripts from all secondary schools attended; and a letter of recommendation from a counselor and/or a teacher. Standardized Test Scores (SAT/ACT) are optional for students applying for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 admission. There are no additional specific application requirements mentioned for the Bachelor in French Language and Literature program.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Department of French and Italian offers undergraduate and graduate programs of study. The French major aims to develop a deep and sophisticated understanding of French and Francophone cultures, literatures, and languages through a range of courses in different historical periods and cultural contexts. It combines a rigorous grounding in French literary and cultural studies with linguistic proficiency. Students majoring in French develop analytical skills that apply to the study of other disciplines as well as their own, and learn to write and speak French with fluency and accuracy. These skills are essential for graduate work in French, in comparative literature, and in other humanities disciplines, and provide a strong basis for careers in international relations, education, journalism, translation, law, or business.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Game Design and Interactive Media
Requirements: Applicants must submit the Common Application with USC Member Questions, the USC Writing Supplement, official transcripts, letters of recommendation (School Report and Counselor Recommendation), and a Mid-Year Report. Standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional. International students must also demonstrate English proficiency. In addition to the general USC application, applicants to the BA in Game Design and Interactive Media must complete a supplemental application and portfolio through SlideRoom, with a $15 fee. The supplemental application is due by December 1 for first-year applicants and February 1 for transfer applicants. The SlideRoom portfolio requires a Game Design Document and a 'Play a Game' submission. Optional portfolio components include a Visual Piece, a Creative Writing Sample, and Additional Information. No prior experience with game design or programming is required.
Department: School of Cinematic Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Game Design and Interactive Media program provides students with the opportunity to specialize in either game design or interactive media. Students gain knowledge of the technical and aesthetic foundations of interactive design as well as the history of interactive media. The curriculum focuses on understanding the foundations of design, developing projects in multidisciplinary teams, and learning how to prototype, produce and iterate designs. Students learn to critically evaluate interactive experiences and develop projects in a range of interactive forms including video games, augmented and virtual reality, interactive installations and more. The game design specialization focuses on game systems and the creation of playable content. The interactive media specialization focuses on designing interactive systems and experiences beyond traditional games including designing for VR/AR, the web, interactive art and installations. Students will complete courses in game design, game production, interactive media and critical studies and complete a senior project.
ScholarshipType: University Merit Scholarships, Athletic Scholarships, Endowed Scholarships, Departmental Scholarships, ROTC Scholarships, Federal Pell Grant, Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant (FSEOG), Cal Grant A, Cal Grant B

Requirements: Applicants must submit The Common Application or Coalition Application, which includes the USC Writing Supplement. Official High School Transcripts are required. Counselor and Teacher Recommendations are optional and may be requested by an admission counselor after initial review. SAT or ACT scores are optional for Fall 2021, Fall 2022, Fall 2023, Fall 2024, Fall 2025 First-Year Applicants. Portfolios are required only for specific majors, such as Architecture, Art, Cinematic Arts, Dance, Design, and Music; Geography is not one of these specified majors.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: Geography is the study of the Earth's landscapes, peoples, places and environments. It is, quite simply, about the world and how we live in it. Geography is a vibrant and diverse field which connects the physical and social sciences, as well as the humanities. It is especially strong as an interdisciplinary field that addresses pressing contemporary problems related to environmental and social change. Geographers study these topics across multiple spatial scales — from the local to the global — and use diverse methods, including quantitative, qualitative, and spatial analysis techniques. A Bachelor of Arts in Geography gives students the tools to understand and engage with real-world problems, such as climate change, natural hazards, urban development, environmental justice, and globalization. Through a combination of coursework, field studies, and research opportunities, students will develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills applicable to a wide range of careers.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based scholarships, Need-based financial aid, Athletic scholarships, ROTC scholarships, Departmental and special programs scholarships, External scholarships

Requirements: The USC application consists of the Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, official transcripts, and letters of recommendation. Applicants may also submit optional SAT or ACT scores, though they are not required for 2024 admission.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Global Studies (BGS) is an interdisciplinary program designed for students interested in understanding and addressing complex global issues. It offers a comprehensive curriculum that integrates political science, economics, sociology, history, and other fields to provide students with a multifaceted perspective on global phenomena. The program emphasizes critical thinking, research skills, and cross-cultural communication, preparing students for careers in international organizations, government, non-profits, and multinational corporations, as well as for further graduate studies. Through a combination of coursework, experiential learning, and opportunities for study abroad, students develop a deep appreciation for diverse cultures and a nuanced understanding of the interconnected challenges facing the world today.

Requirements: First-year applicants to the USC Roski School of Art and Design submit the Common Application with the USC Writing Supplement, high school transcripts, letters of recommendation, and a portfolio. USC is test-optional for Fall 2024 applicants.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, Departmental, Outside Scholarships

Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Chicano/Latino Studies program provides students with the opportunity to explore a variety of disciplines and methodologies concerning Chicana/o and Latina/o culture, history, and social and political life. The undergraduate major draws on diverse fields such as history, literature, political science, sociology, art history, and ethnic studies. At the core of the major are three common courses: an introductory course on the foundations of Chicana/o Latina/o Studies, a course on the social movements and political life of Chicanas/os and Latinas/os, and a course on Chicana/o Latina/o cultural practices. Building on this core, students then select a set of elective courses in consultation with a faculty adviser to deepen their knowledge in one of three areas: Identities, Communities, and the Nation; Transnationalism and Migration; or Race, Class, and Gender. Students are encouraged to develop skills in research, critical thinking, writing, and oral communication through participation in seminars and research projects. In the department’s many courses, students gain a better understanding of the forces that have shaped the lives of Chicanas/os and Latinas/os in the United States and across the Americas, and their contributions to the nation and the world. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for careers in fields such as law, education, public policy, social work, journalism, and community organizing, and for further study in graduate or professional school.

Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: History offers a unique perspective on virtually every dimension of the human experience through time. By exploring the complex roots of contemporary issues, history majors develop the critical thinking, research, and communication skills necessary to navigate a rapidly changing world. They learn to craft compelling narratives from diverse sources, making them adept at analysis, persuasion, and empathy. The Department of History also emphasizes the opportunity to understand other cultures, both past and present, through a variety of different approaches. Faculty research interests are wide-ranging, encompassing ancient, medieval, and modern periods; all major world regions; and many different subfields, including cultural, economic, intellectual, political, social, and gender history.

Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor in Interdisciplinary Studies (BIS) is a highly individualized degree designed for students who have broad intellectual interests and wish to pursue a course of study not offered in existing majors. The BIS program allows students to combine two or three fields of study from different departments, schools or programs, and integrate them into a coherent plan of study. Students complete a total of 128 units and satisfy all general education requirements. The BIS program is administered by the Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences. Students will learn to integrate the knowledge of two or three fields of study. Students will develop an in-depth understanding of the chosen fields of study. Students will develop critical thinking and analytical skills. Students will develop oral and written communication skills.

Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The International Relations major introduces students to the complex and rapidly changing political, economic and socio-cultural processes that connect people and institutions across national borders. The curriculum covers a wide array of topics, including the causes of war and peace, international political economy, foreign policy analysis, human rights, global governance, and regional studies. Students learn to critically analyze major theoretical debates, engage in empirical research, and develop practical skills relevant for careers in diplomacy, international organizations, non-governmental organizations, multinational corporations, and academia. The program offers opportunities for study abroad, internships, and research, preparing students to become informed and engaged global citizens.

Requirements: To apply for first-year admission, please submit the following: Common Application: Complete the Common Application, including the USC Member Questions. Official high school transcripts: Please submit your official high school transcripts. SAT or ACT scores: USC has a test-optional policy for Fall 2024 first-year applicants. Students may apply without submitting SAT or ACT scores. USC Writing Supplement: The USC writing supplement includes one short answer question and one longer essay. Additional supplemental essays may be required for specific programs. Letters of Recommendation: Required: One letter of recommendation from your counselor. Optional: One letter of recommendation from a teacher. Portfolios and interviews: Portfolios are only required for specific programs within the Schools of Architecture, Art and Design, Cinematic Arts, Dance, Dramatic Arts, and Music. Interviews are only required for specific programs within the Schools of Architecture, Cinematic Arts, Dance, Dramatic Arts, and Music.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Concentration: Culture and Society, Economy and Society, Global Governance, Health and the Environment, Peace and Conflict, Religion and International Affairs
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in International Studies provides students with a broad and interdisciplinary understanding of the complex political, economic, social and cultural processes that shape the contemporary world. It prepares students to become globally literate citizens and leaders who can analyze global issues from a variety of perspectives and propose solutions to contemporary problems. The curriculum offers students a firm grounding in the theories, methods and substantive areas of international studies, including global governance, international political economy, international security and peace, global health, and human rights. Students develop critical thinking, research, writing, and language skills that are essential for careers in government, non-governmental organizations, international organizations, business, journalism, and academia.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Italian Language and Literature
Requirements: Common Application, Essays (Common App personal essay + USC Writing Supplement), High School Transcripts, Letters of Recommendation (one), SAT or ACT Scores (Optional for Fall 2024 and 2025), Mid-Year Grade Report.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Italian Major introduces students to the culture and civilization of Italy and provides them with a command of the language and an understanding of its literary and cultural history from the Middle Ages to the present. Courses range from Italian language instruction and conversation to Italian literature and film, history and culture, women's studies, and Renaissance studies. Students are encouraged to develop their interests in fields such as art history, comparative literature, history, and political science, in conjunction with their Italian studies.

Requirements:
Admission to the USC Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism is a two-step process. First, students apply to the University of Southern California (USC). The university reviews all applications for admission. Second, if you are admitted to USC, your application is then forwarded to USC Annenberg for a second review for admission to the school. All prospective students apply using the Common Application. Students applying to Annenberg do not submit a separate application or supplemental materials directly to the school, with the exception of those applying to our Cinematic Arts + Communication, or Design, Technology and Communication Management majors. The general application checklist includes:
1. Common Application (including essays)
2. USC Writing Supplement (USC-specific questions and short answer essays)
3. Official High School Transcripts
4. SAT or ACT Scores (Optional for Fall 2024 and 2025)
5. Letters of Recommendation (One letter of recommendation is required from a counselor or teacher.)
6. Application Fee or Fee Waiver Request
7. Financial Aid Applications (Optional)
Department: USC Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
Description: Are you ready to tell the stories that matter? The Bachelor of Arts in Journalism program at USC Annenberg prepares you to do just that. As a student in our program, you’ll learn from award-winning faculty who are at the forefront of the evolving media landscape. You’ll gain hands-on experience in a variety of media, from traditional print and broadcast to cutting-edge digital platforms. Our curriculum emphasizes ethical storytelling, critical thinking, and multimedia proficiency, ensuring you’re well-equipped for a successful career in journalism. Our curriculum is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of journalism in the 21st century. You’ll develop strong reporting, writing, and editing skills, learn to produce compelling content across different platforms, and explore the ethical dimensions of media. Key areas of study include: Reporting and Writing, Broadcast and Digital Production, Investigative Journalism, Media Ethics and Law, Multimedia Storytelling, Sports Journalism, Photojournalism and Visual Storytelling, Data Journalism, Entrepreneurial Journalism, Arts and Culture Journalism, International Journalism.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Latin and Ancient Greek Studies
Requirements: All students applying for admission to the university must apply online through the Common Application or Coalition Application. First-year applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application with USC Writing Supplement, official high school transcripts, and may submit scores from the SAT or ACT (optional for 2021-2022 applicants and beyond). Transfer applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application with USC Writing Supplement, official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, and official high school transcripts.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Latin and Ancient Greek Studies offers students a unique opportunity to immerse themselves in the rich literary and cultural traditions of ancient Greece and Rome. This interdisciplinary program combines rigorous language training in both Latin and ancient Greek with a comprehensive study of classical literature, history, philosophy, and archaeology. Students will develop advanced linguistic proficiency, critical analytical skills, and a deep understanding of the classical world's enduring legacy. The curriculum is designed to foster intellectual curiosity, independent research abilities, and a nuanced appreciation for the complexities of ancient societies and their profound influence on Western civilization. Graduates will be well-prepared for a variety of career paths, including education, research, museum studies, journalism, law, and other fields requiring strong analytical, communication, and cultural competency skills.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Liberal Arts and Humanities
Requirements: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, High school transcript(s), Mid-Year Report (if applicable), SAT or ACT scores (optional for Fall 2024 applicants), Letters of Recommendation (optional), Portfolio (required for some majors), Audition (required for some majors), English proficiency (if applicable).
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Liberal Arts and Humanities provides students with a broad humanistic education while allowing them to develop disciplinary specialization through their choice of a minor or second major. Students gain intellectual breadth and critical thinking skills by exploring a wide range of subjects, including literature, history, philosophy, and the arts. The program encourages interdisciplinary approaches to complex questions and fosters a deep understanding of diverse cultures and perspectives. Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in fields such as education, journalism, public service, and the arts, as well as for further graduate study.

Requirements:
Required materials for first-year applicants:
*   Common Application: Complete the Common Application, including the USC-specific questions. Your Common Application essay, which is part of the Common Application, is also required.
*   USC Writing Supplement: The USC Writing Supplement is available within the Common Application and consists of one short answer question.
*   High School Transcript(s)
*   SAT or ACT Scores: Reporting SAT or ACT scores is optional for students applying for fall 2024.
*   Letters of Recommendation: One letter of recommendation is required from a counselor or school official. One letter of recommendation from a teacher is strongly recommended.
*   Mid-Year Grades
*   Portfolio, Audition, or Interview: Required only for specific majors and schools.
*   English Proficiency: Required for international students.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Department of Linguistics offers a program leading to the Bachelor of Arts degree. The program is designed to provide students with a general understanding of the nature of language and the methods and results of its study. This program is offered by the Department of Linguistics.

Learning Objectives
All students graduating with a BA in Linguistics will be able to:
* Demonstrate knowledge of the major areas of linguistic analysis (phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, and pragmatics).
* Demonstrate knowledge of the different theoretical frameworks currently used in the study of language.
* Demonstrate knowledge of the different research methods used in the study of language.
* Apply basic linguistic analysis to a variety of linguistic data.
* Demonstrate knowledge of the social, cultural and cognitive aspects of language.

Program Learning Objectives
The major in Linguistics offers students an opportunity to study the nature of language and its relationship to various aspects of human cognition and interaction. The program provides the students with:
* An understanding of the fundamentals of linguistic analysis at various levels (e.g., phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics) and of the main theoretical frameworks and research methods used in the study of language.
* An opportunity to apply basic linguistic analysis to a variety of linguistic data.
* An understanding of the social, cultural, and cognitive aspects of language.
* An understanding of the historical and cross-linguistic variation of language.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Linguistics, Interpretation, and Translation
Requirements: The Common Application and USC Writing Supplement, high school transcript(s), letter(s) of recommendation, and SAT or ACT scores (optional for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 applicants). International students must also demonstrate English proficiency.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: Linguistics is the scientific study of human language. A major in Linguistics provides students with a broad knowledge of language, including its structure, historical development, acquisition, social role, and neurological basis. Students also learn how to apply linguistic knowledge to a variety of practical problems. Linguistics majors develop analytical and critical thinking skills that are highly valued in many careers, including law, medicine, technology, education, and international relations. The Linguistics major also allows students to select one of four concentrations or to pursue a general linguistics track, allowing for customization to suit their interests and career goals.

Requirements:
A first-year applicant is one who has graduated from high school and has not enrolled in a regular session at any college or university. Students who complete college work in the summer immediately following high school graduation are still considered first-year applicants.
Required Application Materials:
* Official high school transcript
* Official SAT/ACT scores (Optional for 2021-2022 and 2022-2023 applicants)
* Letters of recommendation
* Essays
* Optional materials, depending on program
Department: Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor in Management Sciences and Information Systems
Bachelor in Marine Biology and Oceanography
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Marine Biology and Oceanography is offered by the Department of Biological Sciences. This program prepares students for careers in marine sciences and graduate studies in oceanography, marine biology or environmental sciences. The curriculum emphasizes fundamental concepts in biology, chemistry, physics and mathematics, providing a strong scientific foundation relevant to the study of the marine environment. The program includes coursework focused on marine biology, biological oceanography, physical oceanography, chemical oceanography and marine environmental science. Students also gain practical skills through field and laboratory experiences, often involving research opportunities at the USC Wrigley Institute for Environmental Studies on Catalina Island. The program's interdisciplinary nature equips graduates to address complex marine environmental issues and contribute to conservation efforts.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Departmental, Athletic, ROTC, Outside Scholarships

Requirements:
The following materials are required to complete your first-year application to USC:
* Common Application or Coalition Application
* USC Writing Supplement
* Official high school transcripts
* SAT or ACT scores (optional for Fall 2024, 2025, and 2026 applicants)
* Letters of Recommendation (not required but strongly encouraged)
* For certain majors, a portfolio or audition may be required (for example, majors in the Schools of Architecture, Cinematic Arts, Dramatic Arts, or Music).
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: Mathematics is an increasingly important tool in nearly every field of human endeavor. It is the language of science and a fundamental underpinning of technology. Mathematics has an integral role in business, finance, medicine, and government. It has been and continues to be a driving force in intellectual development. The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Mathematics provides students with a broad and deep understanding of mathematics and its applications. It is designed for students seeking a strong foundation in theoretical and applied mathematics, preparing them for graduate studies in mathematics or related fields, or for careers in a wide range of industries. Students will develop analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills, as well as the ability to communicate mathematical ideas effectively. The curriculum covers core areas such as calculus, linear algebra, differential equations, real analysis, complex analysis, abstract algebra, and probability and statistics. Elective courses allow students to explore areas of particular interest, including cryptography, mathematical modeling, numerical analysis, and topology.

Requirements: Common Application (including the USC Writing Supplement); Application Fee or Fee Waiver; Official High School Transcripts; SAT or ACT Scores (Optional for 2024, 2025, and 2026 application cycles); Optional Arts Portfolio or Maker Portfolio
Department: USC Viterbi School of Engineering
Description: Mechanical engineering is one of the most diversified of the engineering disciplines. Mechanical engineers design, develop, build and test mechanical devices, including tools, engines, machines and other equipment. They apply scientific principles in the design, manufacture and maintenance of mechanical systems. Students learn to use computers to aid in the design, analysis, modeling and simulation of complex mechanical engineering systems. The program prepares students for professional careers in industry, research, and government, and for graduate studies.
Accredidation: The undergraduate mechanical engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Minority and Ethnic Studies
Requirements: A complete application includes: The Common Application, including the USC Writing Supplement; Official high school transcripts; Letter(s) of Recommendation. Test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Studies in Race and Ethnicity is an interdisciplinary program designed to address the increasing need for students to think critically about race and ethnicity, especially in our global and technologically advanced society. It offers a broad approach to understanding the complex interrelationships between race, ethnicity, gender, class, and sexuality. Courses analyze the social construction of race and ethnicity, the history of racial and ethnic relations, the impact of race and ethnicity on political and economic systems, and the cultural expressions of different racial and ethnic groups. Students will develop skills in critical thinking, research, and communication, preparing them for a wide range of careers in fields such as education, law, public policy, social justice, and international relations.
ScholarshipType: Need-based, Merit-based, University Scholarships, Departmental Scholarships

Requirements: To complete your application for undergraduate admission to the USC Thornton School of Music, you must submit the following items: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, USC Portfolio (including the USC Thornton School of Music Supplemental Application), Transcripts, Letter(s) of Recommendation, Test Scores, English Proficiency (for international students).
Department: USC Thornton School of Music
Concentration: Composition, Early Music, Guitar (Classical Guitar), Keyboard Collaborative Arts, Keyboard Studies (Piano, Organ, Harpsichord), Music Industry, Orchestral Instruments (Strings, Woodwinds, Brass, Percussion), Vocal Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Music (BM) is a professional degree designed for students who intend to pursue careers in music performance, composition, or other music-related fields. This program emphasizes intensive study in a specific musical area while also providing a broad musical education. Students develop advanced technical skills, artistic expression, and a deep understanding of music theory, history, and literature. The curriculum includes private lessons, ensemble participation, academic music courses, and general education requirements. Graduates are prepared for advanced study, professional careers as performers, composers, educators, and various roles within the music industry.
Accredidation: Institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). The requirements for entrance and for the graduation with degrees in music are in accordance with the published regulations of NASM.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Music History and Literature
Requirements: Applicants must complete the USC application online through the Common Application. The USC application requires essays, high school transcripts, and letters of recommendation. All applicants must also complete the Thornton SlideRoom Submission, which includes submitting two writing samples and a resume. An interview with the department is required. Three letters of recommendation are required, including academic and music references.
Department: Thornton School of Music
Description: This interdisciplinary program, offered jointly by the Thornton School of Music and the Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences, combines intensive study in music history and literature with the general education and specialized study in another field (the major or minor) provided by a liberal arts degree.
