Students develop critical skills by investigating and writing about music and culture within a broader historical context. The program also provides opportunities for study abroad.

Requirements: All applicants to the USC Thornton School of Music must complete two applications: The Common Application (or Coalition Application, powered by Scoir) for USC and The Thornton SlideRoom Application. Required documents for the Common Application include official transcripts from all secondary schools, one academic letter of recommendation (additional letters optional), and essays (USC Writing Supplement and additional questions as prompted by the Common Application). Official SAT or ACT test scores are not required for Fall 2024, 2025, and 2026 admissions, but may be submitted. English proficiency test scores are required for international students. For the Music Industry (B.M.) program, the Thornton SlideRoom Application also requires a detailed music resume, a repertoire list of 2-3 pieces demonstrating proficiency, and a short video introduction (less than 2 minutes) explaining interest in the program and professional goals. Additionally, an interview is required for all applicants to the Music Industry program, conducted virtually over Zoom in January and February.
Department: USC Thornton School of Music
Description: The USC Thornton Bachelor of Music in Music Industry program prepares students for leadership positions in the music industry. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in music, business, and technology, as well as a comprehensive understanding of the evolving legal and financial landscape of the industry. The program emphasizes both theoretical knowledge and practical application, with students gaining hands-on experience through internships and projects.

Requirements: The following items must be submitted by December 1, 2023 for Fall 2024 consideration. Common App or USC Application: All applicants must submit the Common Application or the USC Application online. Application Fee: Pay the $85 USC application fee. Official Transcripts: You must submit official high school transcripts directly to USC. Letters of Recommendation: Letters of Recommendation are not required for Thornton School of Music applicants. Resume/List of Activities: Submit a resume or list of activities via the USC SlideRoom portal (available through your USC Supplemental Application). Supplemental Application: Submit the USC Thornton School of Music Supplemental Application online. The supplemental application is accessible via the USC SlideRoom portal only after you have submitted the Common Application or USC Application. Audition (Live or Recorded): All applicants must successfully complete an audition in their chosen major. See Audition Information. Portfolio (Composition, Screen Scoring, Music Production, Jazz Studies – Instrumental): Portfolio materials are only required for applicants to Composition, Screen Scoring, Music Production, and Jazz Studies (Instrumental). For other majors, disregard portfolio prompts. Writing Sample (Musicology, Music Industry): A writing sample is only required for applicants to Musicology and Music Industry. For other majors, disregard writing sample prompts.
Department: USC Thornton School of Music
Description:
This curriculum prepares students for careers as performing artists, composers and arrangers, church musicians, private instructors and music administrators. Students pursue a rigorous course of study in studio instruction, chamber music, music history and music theory. Additional courses are taken as determined by placement tests and/or adviser recommendations.
In addition to the courses required by the Thornton School of Music for the Bachelor of Music, students must complete the university’s general education requirements.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, USC Trustee, USC Presidential, USC Dean's, Half-Tuition, Full-Tuition

ProgramName: Bachelor in Music Theory and Composition
Department: USC Thornton School of Music
Description: The Bachelor of Music in Composition offers students comprehensive training in music composition, theory, and aural skills, balanced with coursework in history, literature, and general education. The program emphasizes individualized instruction, allowing students to develop their unique compositional voice through private lessons, seminars, and collaborative projects. Students in our programs benefit from a rigorous curriculum that balances traditional training with innovative approaches to music creation. They have ample opportunities to collaborate with performers, conductors, and other artists, both within USC Thornton and across the broader university. Our graduates are highly sought after in the professional world, securing positions in major orchestras, film studios, academic institutions, and independent music organizations. Many also pursue advanced degrees at leading conservatories and universities worldwide.

Department: USC Thornton School of Music

Requirements: To apply as a first-year applicant, you must submit the following: Common Application or Coalition Application, USC Writing Supplement, Official High School Transcripts, Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, SAT/ACT Scores (Optional for fall 2024 applicants). Students applying to USC must meet the following general requirements: Strong academic record with challenging coursework, Competitive grades, Extracurricular activities and leadership experience, Community involvement, Essays and recommendations that highlight unique qualities.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree program in Neuroscience and Neurobiology provides an interdisciplinary approach to the study of the brain and nervous system. Students will gain a strong foundation in the fundamental principles of neuroscience, from the molecular and cellular level to systems and cognitive functions. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, experimental design, data analysis, and scientific communication. Through a combination of rigorous coursework, hands-on laboratory experiences, and research opportunities, students will develop the skills necessary for careers in research, medicine, biotechnology, and other health-related professions, or for advanced graduate studies.

Requirements: First-year applicants must submit: Common Application with USC Writing Supplement, high school transcript(s), counselor recommendation, teacher recommendation, and mid-year school report (if applicable).
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

Requirements: Applicants must submit the Common Application, USC Writing Supplement (Essays and Short Answer Questions), School Report and Counselor Recommendation, Transcripts, and proof of English Proficiency (if applicable). SAT or ACT scores are optional for the 2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024, and 2024-2025 application cycles. For the Bachelor of Arts in Performing Arts program, no supplemental application or audition is required.
Department: School of Cinematic Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Performing Arts is offered by the School of Dramatic Arts. This degree is designed to complement our pre-existing BFA programs and respond to student interest in studying the performing arts in a rigorous liberal arts context, with a specific focus on the intersection of the performing arts with other academic disciplines. Students will explore performance and dramatic literature from an interdisciplinary perspective, gaining historical, theoretical, and practical knowledge in the related fields of theatre, dance, and performance studies. The program will also offer students opportunities to specialize in an area of interest through a capstone project. By engaging in both creative practice and critical inquiry, students will develop a deep understanding of the performing arts and acquire skills that are valuable for a wide range of careers.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Academic major, Talent, Background, Special interest

Requirements: Applicants apply to the BS in Pharmacology & Toxicology program through USC Undergraduate Admissions. First-year applicants must submit: The Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, Official high school transcripts, School Report, Counselor recommendation, Teacher recommendation, and Mid-year report (if applicable). SAT or ACT scores are optional for Fall 2024 applicants.
Department: USC School of Pharmacy
Description: The USC School of Pharmacy is now offering a new undergraduate degree in pharmacology and toxicology — one of only a handful of such programs in the nation. The Bachelor in Pharmacology and Toxicology will train students for careers in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, government, and academic sectors, as well as for further graduate studies in pharmacology, toxicology, medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, and law. Students will gain expertise in areas such as drug discovery, development, regulation, and therapeutic applications, as well as the study of harmful effects of chemicals on living systems. The new program offers a strong foundation in the basic sciences, including biology, chemistry, and mathematics, and then progresses to advanced coursework in pharmacology, toxicology, molecular biology, and medicinal chemistry. Beyond foundational science, the curriculum includes courses in pharmacology, pharmacogenomics, neuropharmacology, molecular and biochemical toxicology, forensic toxicology, and drug discovery and development. The program culminates in a senior research project or an internship, providing hands-on experience and opportunities to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world problems. The degree also prepares students for professional programs (M.D., Pharm.D., D.D.S., Ph.D. and J.D.). Students in the new program will benefit from the school’s strong research environment and faculty expertise in drug discovery, experimental therapeutics, clinical pharmacology, and regulatory science. They will also have opportunities to participate in research with faculty mentors and gain valuable laboratory experience. The school is home to state-of-the-art research facilities, including the USC Center for Drug Discovery and Development, the USC Center for Genomic and Experimental Medicine, and the USC Regulatory Science program.

Requirements: First-year applicants must complete the Common Application or Coalition Application online. These applications provide biographical information, information about academic history, extracurricular activities, and written essays. Required documents include: Common Application or Coalition Application, official high school transcripts, official SAT or ACT scores (if applicable), recommendations (counselor and teacher), and essays. Portfolio, writing sample, and/or other supplements may be required for certain majors (if applicable). Financial aid applications are required only if the student is applying for financial assistance.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The undergraduate program in philosophy at USC is designed to provide students with a broad and rigorous training in the field. The program aims to give students both historical and systematic perspectives on philosophy, and to enable them to develop their capacities for critical thinking, logical analysis, and precise articulation. Students are encouraged to explore a wide range of philosophical issues and traditions, and to engage with contemporary debates in the field. The curriculum is structured to ensure a solid foundation in core areas of philosophy, while also allowing for specialization in particular areas of interest.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Leadership, Artistic talent, Athletic skill, Affiliation with certain organizations

Requirements: All applicants must submit the Common Application and the USC Writing Supplement. The USC Writing Supplement includes short answer questions and essays. First-year applicants must submit: Common App application, USC Writing Supplement, Counselor recommendation, Teacher recommendation, High school transcript, SAT or ACT scores (optional for Fall 2024, Fall 2025, and Fall 2026 applicants). Portfolio (required for some arts programs) and Interview (required for some arts and scholarship programs) are not applicable to the Bachelor in Physics program. International students may have additional requirements, such as English proficiency exams.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Physics provides a comprehensive education in fundamental physics. The program offers a strong foundation for graduate studies in physics and related fields and for careers in industry or secondary education. The program meets the needs of students interested in a physics-intensive education.

Requirements: Admission to the School of Cinematic Arts for all undergraduate programs is highly competitive and is based on a review of the applicant’s academic record, writing samples for students applying to Writing, Critical Studies, Animation, and Film & Television Production, and an interview for students applying to Film & Television Production and Interactive Media. Students applying to the BA in Cinematic Arts program are required to submit an essay.
Department: School of Cinematic Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts degree with a major in Writing for Screen and Television is designed to provide students with the strongest possible foundation for professional writing careers in screen and television. The program combines an intensive and varied curriculum in the art and craft of writing for the screen with a thorough background in the liberal arts. The program's faculty consists of working professional writers, deeply committed to teaching students the critical and professional skills that will enable them to develop their voices and abilities as writers. The curriculum is constantly evolving in response to the changes in the entertainment industry. Students develop writing skills across a range of formats, including features, television, and web series, and learn about the foundations of story, character, structure, and theme. The program is designed to provide a complete undergraduate education for students with the talent and ambition to become professional screenwriters and television writers.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Political Science and Government
Requirements: All first-year applicants must submit the Common Application, USC Writing Questions, high school transcript(s), and letter(s) of recommendation. A Mid-Year Report is also required if available. Standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 applicants.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Political Science and Government program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of political systems, institutions, and behavior. Students will develop critical thinking skills, analytical abilities, and a deep knowledge of political theory, comparative politics, international relations, and American politics. The curriculum prepares students for a wide range of careers in government, non-profit organizations, law, journalism, business, and academia, as well as for advanced graduate study.

Requirements:
All applicants should submit the following:
*   Common Application
*   USC Writing Supplement
*   Official High School Transcripts
*   School Report and Counselor Recommendation
*   Mid-Year School Report (if applicable)

Additional Materials:
*   Teacher Recommendation (optional): We welcome one letter of recommendation from a teacher, particularly one who taught you in a core academic subject area (English, mathematics, science, social studies, foreign language). Please request letters from teachers who know you well and can speak to your strengths and readiness for a rigorous academic environment.
*   Standardized Test Scores (optional for Fall 2024 first-year applicants): USC does not require SAT or ACT scores for Fall 2024 first-year applicants. However, if you have taken the SAT or ACT and wish to submit your scores, you may do so. Submitted scores will be considered in the context of the rest of your application and will not be used to your disadvantage.

Portfolio or Audition:
Some majors require a portfolio or audition as part of the application. Please check our list of majors with additional requirements to see if your intended major requires a portfolio or audition.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The undergraduate program in psychology is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the scientific study of behavior and mental processes. Students gain knowledge across various subfields of psychology, including cognitive, developmental, social, clinical, and biological psychology. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, research methods, and statistical analysis, preparing students for diverse career paths or further graduate studies in psychology or related fields. Graduates will be equipped to analyze complex psychological issues, design and interpret research, and apply psychological principles to real-world problems.

Department: USC Price School of Public Policy
Description:
The Bachelor in Public Policy Analysis (PPA) is designed for students committed to careers that address critical public issues and challenges in public, private and nonprofit sectors. The program provides the necessary background for students interested in a wide range of policy areas, including health, education, the environment, criminal justice, economic development, social welfare and urban planning. The PPA program offers students the opportunity to learn about important policy problems, how to analyze those problems, and how to create solutions. Students are prepared for immediate entry into professional careers, for graduate studies in public policy and administration, or for law school.
Public Policy Analysis Learning Objectives:
Students will be able to:
* Describe the structure and functions of governmental institutions and their role in the policy process.
* Identify current public policy problems and their social, political and economic context.
* Apply economic principles, quantitative reasoning, and public finance tools to analyze public policy problems.
* Explain ethical concerns and concepts related to public policy.
* Articulate effective policy solutions for domestic and international problems.
* Demonstrate written and oral communication skills appropriate for policy analysis and professional careers.

Requirements: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, Official high school transcripts, Letters of recommendation, SAT or ACT scores (Optional for Fall 2024), Optional materials: portfolio (art, architecture, cinematic arts, dance, music, theatre).
Department: USC Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism

Requirements: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement (including two short answer questions and one essay), High School Transcript, School Report and Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, Standardized Test Scores (Optional).
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Religion major provides students with knowledge about the world's diverse religious traditions through an interdisciplinary approach that considers religion in historical, social, political, and cultural contexts. Students learn critical thinking skills as they interpret religious texts and practices, analyze different theories of religion, and engage in informed discussions about topics such as religious diversity, ethics, and the role of religion in public life. The major prepares students for a wide range of careers in fields such as education, law, journalism, public service, non-profit organizations, and religious leadership.
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, leadership, special talents, athletic, special interest

ProgramName: Bachelor in Russian and Eastern European Languages and Literature
Requirements:
We offer two admission plans for first-year applicants: Early Action and Regular Decision. Our admission decisions are based on a holistic review of your application, which includes your academic record, essays, letters of recommendation, extracurricular activities, and other achievements.
Application Checklist:
Common Application with USC Writing Supplement
Application Fee or Fee Waiver
Official High School Transcripts
SAT/ACT Scores (Optional for 2024, 2025, and 2026 application cycles)
Letters of Recommendation (Optional)
TOEFL/IELTS/PTE Academic (required for international students)
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Freshman Scholarships, Transfer Scholarships, Departmental Scholarships, USC Army ROTC Scholarships

ProgramName: Bachelor in Social Science Research Methods
Requirements: To apply to USC, first-year applicants must submit the following: Common Application, USC Writing Supplement, Official high school transcripts, Scores from the SAT or ACT (if you choose to submit them), Optional: letters of recommendation, Optional: portfolio or creative submission (for specific majors). Deadline for all materials: December 1, 2023.
Department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Social Sciences with an Emphasis in Economics is a multi-disciplinary major designed for students who want to develop a deeper understanding of human behavior in a social and economic context. Students will take courses in economics, political science, sociology, psychology and related fields. This major provides students with a strong foundation in quantitative methods and data analysis, preparing them for careers in a wide range of fields, including business, government, and non-profit organizations. Students will also be well-prepared for graduate study in social sciences or related professional fields.

Requirements: Common Application or Coalition Application, USC Writing Supplement (including short answer questions and one extended essay), Official high school transcripts, Counselor recommendation, Teacher recommendation.
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: Sociology is the scientific study of social behavior, social groups, and human society. It focuses on the patterns and dynamics of social relationships, the organization of social life, and the causes and consequences of social change. The Department of Sociology trains students to develop their sociological imagination, to analyze the social world in a critical and rigorous manner, and to understand the relevance of sociology for their own lives and for creating a more just and equitable society.
ScholarshipType: Academic Merit, Financial Need, Federal and State Grants, Departmental, Athletic

ProgramName: Bachelor in Spanish Language and Literature
Department: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Description: The Department of Latin American and Iberian Cultures provides undergraduate students with the opportunity to pursue studies in Spanish language and literature. The department offers a Bachelor of Arts in Spanish Language and Literature. Courses cover Spanish and Latin American literature, culture, linguistics and film. Students are also encouraged to study abroad.
ScholarshipType: Academic Merit, Talent, Leadership, Financial Need

Requirements: Admission to all programs in the Roski School of Art and Design is contingent on admission to the university. General university admission for first-year applicants requires: USC Application, Essay (which includes a writing supplement with prompts and several short answer questions), Test Scores (SAT/ACT are optional for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 applicants), High School Transcript(s), and Letter(s) of Recommendation. For the Bachelor in Studio Arts program, applicants must also submit a portfolio of creative work consisting of 10–20 images or up to 10 minutes of time-based work through SlideRoom.
Department: Roski School of Art and Design
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) in Studio Arts is a four-year, pre-professional degree designed to provide focused, in-depth study of contemporary art practices and theory. In the first two years of the program, students take a core curriculum that provides a broad foundation in different visual art media, concepts, and theories. Courses emphasize art fundamentals and critical thinking in addition to gaining a wide range of technical skills. As students progress, they focus on more advanced critical, historical, and theoretical approaches in the production of art and will develop a specialization in a chosen area of study. The curriculum allows students the opportunity to learn from and work with faculty who are active, exhibiting artists. The curriculum culminates with the completion of a capstone experience through a solo exhibition and an artist statement/research paper.

Requirements: Undergraduate applicants apply to the university through the USC Undergraduate Admission office. In addition to the university application, applicants must also complete a supplemental application through the School of Dramatic Arts. All applicants who are invited to an interview/audition/portfolio review will be notified via email approximately three to four weeks prior to the scheduled date.
Department: School of Dramatic Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre Design provides intensive professional training for students desiring careers in scenic design, costume design, lighting design or sound design for theatre, film or television. The program develops knowledgeable and creative artists by providing a strong foundation in design principles and technology while encouraging individual artistic expression. The curriculum features an intensive sequence of studio classes, including scene design, costume design, lighting design, sound design and digital design tools, supplemented by courses in theatre history, dramatic literature and performance studies. The program is designed to provide students with the skills and theoretical background necessary to develop a professional design career. Students completing this degree will be prepared for a variety of entry-level positions in the entertainment industry and for continued graduate studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Urban Studies and Affairs
Department: Price School of Public Policy
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Urban Studies and Planning prepares students to address crucial issues facing urban areas. Through an interdisciplinary curriculum grounded in social sciences, students will learn to analyze urban problems from a spatial perspective, understand the processes of urban change, and develop innovative solutions for a more sustainable and equitable future. The program emphasizes critical thinking, research methods, and practical skills in areas such as geographic information systems (GIS), data analysis, and policy formulation. Graduates are equipped for careers in urban planning, policy analysis, community development, real estate, and environmental management, or for further graduate studies in related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor in Visual and Performing Arts
Requirements: To apply to USC as a freshman for fall or spring, you will need to submit: Common Application, including the personal essay; USC Writing Supplement; Official High School Transcripts; Letter of Recommendation (from a counselor or a teacher); Standardized Test Scores (optional for applicants applying for the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 application cycles). A Mid-Year Report is required. Portfolios are required for specific majors only.

Applicants must submit the Common Application (including essay and USC short answer questions), official high school transcripts, and letters of recommendation (one from a high school counselor and one from a high school teacher). A supplemental application to the USC Thornton School of Music is also required, which includes an audition. Thornton encourages additional letters of recommendation from music teachers/mentors. An optional resume/CV and an optional personal statement/essay may be uploaded with the supplemental application. SAT or ACT scores are optional for Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 applicants.
Department: Thornton School of Music
Description: The Bachelor of Music in Voice and Opera prepares students for professional careers as opera singers and for graduate study. This program of study develops the highest level of singing technique and comprehensive musicianship, together with a broad knowledge of opera and song literature in all languages. Students receive extensive coaching and performance experience in USC Thornton opera productions, as well as in the areas of early music, art song, and new music. All voice students are required to participate in at least one ensemble each semester; for most voice majors this will be a choral or opera ensemble.
